“Indeed, having good expectations of Allah is part of excellent worship of Allah.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4993), al-Tirmidhī (3604), Aḥmad (7956), and Ibn Ḥibbān (631).

١٥٧ — عن أم العلاء رضي الله عنها — امرأة من الأنصار بايعت النبي ﷺ — أنها أخبرته أنه اقتُسم المهاجرون قرعة، فطار لنا عثمان بن مظعون، فأنزلناه في أبياتنا، فوجع وجعه الذي توفي فيه.
فلما توفي وغُسل وكُفن في أثوابه، دخل رسول الله ﷺ، فقلت:
رحمة الله عليك أبا السائب، فشهادتي عليك لقد أكرمك الله.
فقال النبي ﷺ:
«وما يدريك أن الله أكرمه؟»
فقلت:
بأبي أنت يا رسول الله، فمن يكرمه الله؟
فقال:
«أما هو فقد جاءه اليقين، والله إني لأرجو له الخير، والله ما أدري وأنا رسول الله ما يُفعل بي».
قالت:
فوالله لا أزكي أحداً بعده أبداً.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٢٤٣).

157 — Umm al-ʿAlāʾ may Allah be pleased with her, a woman of the Anṣār who had pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ, reported:
The Muhājirūn were distributed among the Anṣār by drawing lots, and ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn fell to our share. We accommodated him in our homes, and he became afflicted with the illness from which he eventually died.
When he died, had been washed, and was wrapped in his burial shrouds, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered.
I said:
“May Allah have mercy upon you, O Abū al-Sāʾib. My testimony concerning you is that Allah has certainly honored you.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“How do you know that Allah has honored him?”
I said:
“May my father be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah. Then whom will Allah honor?”
He replied:
“As for him, certainty — death — has come to him. By Allah, I certainly hope for good for him. Yet by Allah, I do not know, even though I am the Messenger of Allah, what will be done with me.”
She said:
“By Allah, after that I never again declared anyone with certainty to be righteous before Allah.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1243).

بأبي أنت يا رسول الله، فمن يكرمه الله؟
فقال:
«أما هو فقد جاءه اليقين، والله إني لأرجو له الخير، والله ما أدري وأنا رسول الله ما يُفعل بي».
قالت:
فوالله لا أزكي أحداً بعده أبداً.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٢٤٣).
157 — Umm al-ʿAlāʾ may Allah be pleased with her, a woman of the Anṣār who had pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ, reported:
The Muhājirūn were distributed among the Anṣār by drawing lots, and ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn fell to our share. We accommodated him in our homes, and he became afflicted with the illness from which he eventually died.
When he died, had been washed, and was wrapped in his burial shrouds, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered.
I said:
“May Allah have mercy upon you, O Abū al-Sāʾib. My testimony concerning you is that Allah has certainly honored you.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“How do you know that Allah has honored him?”
I said:
“May my father be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah. Then whom will Allah honor?”
He replied:
“As for him, certainty — death — has come to him. By Allah, I certainly hope for good for him. Yet by Allah, I do not know, even though I am the Messenger of Allah, what will be done with me.”
She said:
“By Allah, after that I never again declared anyone with certainty to be righteous before Allah.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1243).

١٥٨ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ:
«أن رجلاً كان قبلكم رغسه الله مالاً، فقال لبنيه لما حُضر: أي أب كنت لكم؟
قالوا: خير أب.
قال: فإني لم أعمل خيراً قط، فإذا مت فأحرقوني، ثم اسحقوني، ثم ذروني في يوم عاصف.
ففعلوا، فجمعه الله عز وجل، فقال: ما حملك؟
قال: مخافتك.
فتلقاه برحمته».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٤٧٨)، ومسلم (٢٧٥٧).
وقوله:
«رغسه»
أي: أعطاه وبارك له فيه، من الرغس، وهو البركة والنماء والخير.
وقوله:
«اسحقوني»
من السحق، وهو أشد الدق.

158 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“There was a man among those before you whom Allah had granted abundant wealth.
When death approached him, he said to his sons:
‘What kind of father have I been to you?’
They replied:
‘The best of fathers.’
He said:
‘I have never performed any good deed. When I die, burn me, then crush me thoroughly, and afterward scatter me on a violently windy day.’
They did so.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gathered him and asked:
‘What caused you to do this?’
He replied:
‘Fear of You.’
So Allah received him with His mercy.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3478) and Muslim (2757).
The expression «رغسه الله مالاً» means that Allah gave him abundant wealth and placed blessing in it. The word al-raghs denotes blessing, growth, and abundant good.
The expression «اسحقوني» means: crush or grind me extremely finely.

١٥٩ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«قال رجل لم يعمل حسنة قط لأهله: إذا مات فحرقوه، ثم اذروا نصفه في البر ونصفه في البحر، فوالله لئن قدر الله عليه ليعذبنه عذاباً لا يعذبه أحداً من العالمين.
فلما مات الرجل فعلوا ما أمرهم به، فأمر الله البر فجمع ما فيه، وأمر البحر فجمع ما فيه، ثم قال: لم فعلت هذا؟
قال: من خشيتك يا رب، وأنت أعلم.
قال: فغفر له».
متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٥٢)، والبخاري (٧٥٠٦)، ومسلم (٢٧٥٦).

english_source:
159 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“A man who had never performed a good deed said to his family:
‘When I die, burn me. Then scatter half of me upon the land and half of me into the sea. By Allah, if Allah gets hold of me, He will surely punish me with a punishment unlike that with which He has punished anyone else among the worlds.’
When the man died, they did as he had commanded them.
Allah commanded the land to gather what was within it, and He commanded the sea to gather what was within it.
Then He asked:
‘Why did you do this?’
The man replied:
‘Out of fear of You, my Lord, and You know best.’
So Allah forgave him.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik (52), al-Bukhārī (7506), and Muslim (2756).

١٦٠ — عن عقبة قال:
قال لحذيفة:
ألا تحدثنا ما سمعت من النبي ﷺ؟
قال:
سمعته يقول:
«إن رجلاً حضره الموت، فلما أيس من الحياة أوصى أهله: إذا مت فأجمعوا لي حطباً كثيراً، ثم أوروا ناراً، حتى إذا أكلت لحمي وخلصت إلى عظمي، فخذوها فاطحنوها، ثم انظروا يوماً راحاً فاذروه في اليم.
فجمعه الله، فقال: لم فعلت؟
قال: خشيتك.
فغفر له».
قال عقبة:
وأنا سمعته يقول.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٤٧٩).

160 — ʿUqbah reported:
He said to Ḥudhayfah:
“Will you not tell us what you heard from the Prophet ﷺ?”
Ḥudhayfah replied:
I heard him say:
“A man was approached by death. When he despaired of remaining alive, he instructed his family:
‘When I die, gather a great quantity of firewood for me and kindle a fire. When the fire has consumed my flesh and reached my bones, take my remains and grind them. Then wait for a very windy day and scatter them into the sea.’
Allah then gathered him and asked:
‘Why did you do this?’
He replied:
‘Out of fear of You.’
So Allah forgave him.”
ʿUqbah said:
“And I too heard him say it.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3479).

١٦١ — عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله تعالى:
﴿لَا إِكْرَاهَ فِي الدِّينِ﴾
 [البقرة: ٢٥٦]
قال:
كانت المرأة من الأنصار لا يكاد يعيش لها ولد، فتحلف لئن عاش لها ولد لتهودنه. فلما أُجليت بنو النضير، إذا فيهم ناس من أبناء الأنصار.
فقالت الأنصار:
يا رسول الله، أبناؤنا!
فأنزل الله هذه الآية:
﴿لَا إِكْرَاهَ فِي الدِّينِ﴾.
قال سعيد بن جبير:
فمن شاء لحق بهم، ومن شاء دخل في الإسلام.
صحيح: رواه ابن حبان في صحيحه (١٤٠)، وأبو داود (٢٦٨٢).
وفي رواية أبي داود:
«كانت المرأة تكون مِقْلاتاً، فتجعل على نفسها إن عاش لها ولد أن تهوده».
وقوله: «مِقْلاتاً»؛ قال أبو داود: هي التي لا يعيش لها ولد.

١٦١ — عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله تعالى:
﴿لَا إِكْرَاهَ فِي الدِّينِ﴾
 [البقرة: ٢٥٦]
قال:
كانت المرأة من الأنصار لا يكاد يعيش لها ولد، فتحلف لئن عاش لها ولد لتهودنه. فلما أُجليت بنو النضير، إذا فيهم ناس من أبناء الأنصار.
فقالت الأنصار:
يا رسول الله، أبناؤنا!
فأنزل الله هذه الآية:
﴿لَا إِكْرَاهَ فِي الدِّينِ﴾.
قال سعيد بن جبير:
فمن شاء لحق بهم، ومن شاء دخل في الإسلام.
صحيح: رواه ابن حبان في صحيحه (١٤٠)، وأبو داود (٢٦٨٢).
وفي رواية أبي داود:
«كانت المرأة تكون مِقْلاتاً، فتجعل على نفسها إن عاش لها ولد أن تهوده».
وقوله: «مِقْلاتاً»؛ قال أبو داود: هي التي لا يعيش لها ولد.
english_source:
161 — Ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them said concerning the words of Allah Most High:
“There is no compulsion in religion.”
 [Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:256]
A woman from the Anṣār would have children who rarely survived. She would therefore vow that if a child of hers survived, she would raise him as a Jew.
When Banū al-Naḍīr were expelled, there were among them some sons of the Anṣār.
The Anṣār said:
“O Messenger of Allah, our sons!”
Allah then revealed:
“There is no compulsion in religion.”
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said:
“Whoever wished could join them, and whoever wished could enter Islam.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ (140) and Abū Dāwūd (2682).
In the wording of Abū Dāwūd:
“A woman would be miqlāt, so she would vow that if a child of hers survived, she would make him a Jew.”
Abū Dāwūd explained that «مِقْلاتاً» means a woman whose children do not survive.

١٦٢ — عن أنس رضي الله عنه:
أن النبي ﷺ قال لرجل:
«أَسْلِمْ».
قال:
إني أجدني كارهاً.
قال:
«وإن كنت كارهاً».
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٢٠٦١، ١٢٨٦٨).
وليس في الحديث ما يدل على إكراهه على الإسلام، بل النبي ﷺ دعاه إلى الإسلام، فأخبر أن نفسه ليست قابلة له، بل هي كارهة، فقال له:
«أَسْلِمْ وإن كنت كارهاً».
فإن الله سيرزقك حسن النية والإخلاص. قاله ابن كثير في تفسيره.

english_source:
162 — Anas may Allah be pleased with him reported:
The Prophet ﷺ said to a man:
“Accept Islam.”
The man replied:
“I find myself disliking it.”
He said:
“Even if you dislike it.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Aḥmad (12061, 12868).
There is nothing in this ḥadīth indicating that the man was forced to embrace Islam. Rather, the Prophet ﷺ invited him to Islam, and the man explained that inwardly he did not yet feel inclined toward it but instead felt reluctant.
The Prophet ﷺ therefore told him:
“Accept Islam, even if you dislike it,”
for Allah would grant him good intention and sincerity. This was explained by Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr.

١٦٣ — عن الأحنف بن قيس قال:
ذهبت لأنصر هذا الرجل — يعني علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه — فلقيني أبو بكرة رضي الله عنه فقال:
أين تريد؟
قلت:
أنصر هذا الرجل.
قال:
ارجع، فإني سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«إذا التقى المسلمان بسيفيهما فالقاتل والمقتول في النار».
فقلت:
يا رسول الله، هذا القاتل، فما بال المقتول؟
قال:
«إنه كان حريصاً على قتل صاحبه».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣١)، ومسلم (٢٨٨٨).

163 — Al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays reported:
I went out intending to support this man — meaning ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib may Allah be pleased with him — when Abū Bakrah may Allah be pleased with him met me and asked:
“Where are you going?”
I replied:
“To support this man.”
He said:
“Go back, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘When two Muslims confront one another with their swords, both the killer and the one killed are in the Fire.’”
I asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, this is understandable concerning the killer, but what about the one who was killed?”
He replied:
“He was eager to kill his companion.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (31) and Muslim (2888).

١٦٤ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«سباب المسلم فسوق، وقتاله كفر».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٨)، ومسلم (٦٤).
وقوله: «قتاله كفر»؛ قال البغوي في شرح السنة (١٣/١٣٠):
«إنما هو على أن يستبيح دمه، ولا يرى الإسلام عاصماً لدمه، فهذا منه ردة وحقيقة كفر. وقد يجعل ذلك على تشبيه أفعالهم بأفعال الكفار دون حقيقة الكفر إذا قتله غير مستبيح لدمه، كما قال:
“لا ترجعوا بعدي كفاراً يضرب بعضكم رقاب بعض”،
أي: لا تكونوا من الذين عادتهم ذلك».

164 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Insulting a Muslim is sinful disobedience, and fighting him is disbelief.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (48) and Muslim (64).
Regarding the words, “fighting him is disbelief,” al-Baghawī said in Sharḥ al-Sunnah (13/130):
“This applies as actual disbelief when a person regards the blood of a Muslim as lawful and does not regard Islam as protecting his life. In that case, it constitutes apostasy and genuine disbelief.
It may also mean that such conduct resembles the actions of the disbelievers without being actual disbelief when the person kills him without regarding his blood as lawful, just as the Prophet ﷺ said:
‘Do not return after me as disbelievers, striking the necks of one another.’
That is: do not become like those whose habitual conduct is such.”

«إنما هو على أن يستبيح دمه، ولا يرى الإسلام عاصماً لدمه، فهذا منه ردة وحقيقة كفر. وقد يجعل ذلك على تشبيه أفعالهم بأفعال الكفار دون حقيقة الكفر إذا قتله غير مستبيح لدمه، كما قال:
“لا ترجعوا بعدي كفاراً يضرب بعضكم رقاب بعض”،
أي: لا تكونوا من الذين عادتهم ذلك».
164 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Insulting a Muslim is sinful disobedience, and fighting him is disbelief.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (48) and Muslim (64).
Regarding the words, “fighting him is disbelief,” al-Baghawī said in Sharḥ al-Sunnah (13/130):
“This applies as actual disbelief when a person regards the blood of a Muslim as lawful and does not regard Islam as protecting his life. In that case, it constitutes apostasy and genuine disbelief.
It may also mean that such conduct resembles the actions of the disbelievers without being actual disbelief when the person kills him without regarding his blood as lawful, just as the Prophet ﷺ said:
‘Do not return after me as disbelievers, striking the necks of one another.’
That is: do not become like those whose habitual conduct is such.”

١٦٧ — عن زيد بن خالد الجهني رضي الله عنه قال:
صلى لنا رسول الله ﷺ صلاة الصبح بالحديبية على إثر سماء كانت من الليل، فلما انصرف أقبل على الناس فقال:
«أتدرون ماذا قال ربكم؟»
قالوا:
الله ورسوله أعلم.
قال:
«قال: أصبح من عبادي مؤمن بي وكافر بي. فأما من قال: مُطرنا بفضل الله ورحمته، فذلك مؤمن بي، كافر بالكوكب. وأما من قال: مُطرنا بنوء كذا وكذا، فذلك كافر بي، مؤمن بالكوكب».
متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٤)، والبخاري (٨٤٦)، ومسلم (٧١).
وقوله: «النوء»؛ قال ابن الصلاح:
«في أصله ليس نفس الكوكب، فإنه مصدر ناء النجم ينوء نوءاً، أي سقط وغاب، وقيل: نهض وطلع».
ثم قال:
«ثم إن النجم نفسه قد يسمى نوءاً تسمية للفاعل بالمصدر».
وقال أبو إسحاق الزجاج في بعض أماليه:
«الساقطة في المغرب هي الأنواء، والطالع في المشرق هو الرقيب».
صيانة صحيح مسلم (ص ٢٤٦–٢٤٧).

167 — Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī may Allah be pleased with him reported:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the dawn prayer at al-Ḥudaybiyyah following rainfall that had occurred during the night.
When he finished the prayer, he turned toward the people and asked:
“Do you know what your Lord has said?”
They replied:
“Allah and His Messenger know best.”
He said:
“He said: ‘This morning some of My servants have become believers in Me and others disbelievers in Me. As for the one who said, “We were given rain by the grace of Allah and His mercy,” he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the star. But as for the one who said, “We were given rain by such-and-such nawʾ,” he is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the star.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik (4), al-Bukhārī (846), and Muslim (71).
Regarding the word «النوء», Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ said:
“Originally, it does not refer to the star itself. Rather, it is the verbal noun of the expression nāʾa al-najm, meaning that the star set and disappeared; and it has also been said to mean that it rose and appeared.”
He then said:
“The star itself may subsequently be called nawʾ, the doer being named by the verbal noun.”
Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj said in some of his dictations that the stars setting in the west are called the anwāʾ, while the corresponding star rising in the east is its raqīb.
Ṣiyānat Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, pp. 246–247.

١٦٨ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«ألم تروا إلى ما قال ربكم؟ قال: ما أنعمت على عبادي من نعمة إلا أصبح فريق منهم بها كافرين، يقولون: الكواكب، وبالكواكب».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٧٢).
وزاد في رواية:
«ما أنزل الله من السماء من بركة إلا أصبح فريق من الناس بها كافرين، ينزل الله الغيث فيقولون: الكوكب كذا وكذا».

168 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Have you not considered what your Lord said? He said: ‘I do not bestow any blessing upon My servants except that a group among them enters the morning disbelieving in it, saying: The stars, and because of the stars.’”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (72).
Another narration adds:
“Allah does not send down any blessing from the sky except that a group of people enters the morning disbelieving in it. Allah sends down the rain, and they say: ‘Such-and-such star caused it.’”

١٦٩ — عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال:
مُطر الناس على عهد النبي ﷺ، فقال النبي ﷺ:
«أصبح من الناس شاكر، ومنهم كافر؛ هذه رحمة الله، وقال بعضهم: لقد صدق نوء كذا وكذا».
فنزلت هذه الآيات:
﴿فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِمَوَاقِعِ النُّجُومِ ۝ وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ ۝ إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ ۝ فِي كِتَابٍ مَكْنُونٍ ۝ لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ ۝ تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ۝ أَفَبِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ أَنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ ۝ وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾
 [الواقعة: ٧٥–٨٢]
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٧٣).

english_source:
169 — Ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them reported:
Rain fell upon the people during the time of the Prophet ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“This morning some of the people became grateful and some became disbelievers. Some said, ‘This is the mercy of Allah,’ while others said, ‘Such-and-such nawʾ has proven true.’”
Then these verses were revealed:
“Then I swear by the positions of the stars — and indeed, it is a tremendous oath, if you only knew — indeed, this is truly a noble Qurʾān, in a well-preserved Book, touched by none except the purified, a revelation from the Lord of all worlds. Is it this message that you take lightly, and do you make your provision that you deny it?”
 [Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah 56:75–82]
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (73).

١٧٠ — عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه قال:
قحط المطر على عهد رسول الله ﷺ، فسألنا نبي الله ﷺ أن يستسقي لنا، فاستسقى.
فغدا نبي الله ﷺ، فإذا هو بقوم يتحدثون، قالوا:
سُقينا الليلة بنوء كذا وكذا.
فقال نبي الله ﷺ:
«ما أنعم الله على قوم نعمة إلا أصبحوا بها كافرين».
حسن: رواه البزار (٤١٠٢)، والطبراني في مسند الشاميين (١١٠٢).

english_source:
170 — Abū al-Dardāʾ may Allah be pleased with him reported:
Rain became scarce during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so we asked the Prophet of Allah ﷺ to pray for rain for us, and he did so.
The next morning, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came upon some people who were speaking together.
They said:
“We were given rain last night because of such-and-such nawʾ.”
The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
“Allah does not bestow a blessing upon a people except that some of them enter the morning disbelieving in that blessing.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Bazzār (4102) and al-Ṭabarānī in Musnad al-Shāmiyyīn (1102).

١٧٢ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه:
أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«ثلاث من عمل أهل الجاهلية لا يتركهن أهل الإسلام: النياحة، والاستسقاء بالأنواء، وكذا».
قال الراوي:
قلت لسعيد:
وما هو؟
قال:
«دعوى الجاهلية: يا آل فلان، يا آل فلان».
حسن: رواه أحمد (٧٥٦٠)، وصححه ابن حبان (٣١٤١).

172 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Three practices from the deeds of the pre-Islamic period will not be abandoned by the people of Islam: wailing over the dead, seeking rain through attribution to the anwāʾ, and such-and-such.”
The narrator said:
I asked Saʿīd:
“What is the other practice?”
He replied:
“The tribal call of the pre-Islamic period: ‘O family of so-and-so! O family of so-and-so!’”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Aḥmad (7560), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (3141).

١٧٣ — عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما:
أن ناساً من أهل الشرك كانوا قد قتلوا فأكثروا، وزنوا فأكثروا، فأتوا محمداً ﷺ فقالوا:
إن الذي تقول وتدعو إليه لحسن، لو تخبرنا أن لما عملنا كفارة.
فنزلت:
﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا يَزْنُونَ﴾
 [الفرقان: ٦٨]
ونزل:
﴿قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللهِ﴾
 [الزمر: ٥٣]
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٨١٠)، ومسلم (١٢٢).

Some people from among the polytheists had committed much killing and had repeatedly committed unlawful sexual relations.
They came to Muḥammad ﷺ and said:
“What you say and call people toward is certainly good, if only you could tell us whether there is any expiation for what we have done.”
Then Allah revealed:
“And those who do not invoke another deity alongside Allah, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except with legal right, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse…”
 [Sūrat al-Furqān 25:68]
And He revealed:
“Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah.”
 [Sūrat al-Zumar 39:53]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4810) and Muslim (122).

١٧٤ — عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال:
قال رجل:
يا رسول الله، أنؤاخذ بما عملنا في الجاهلية؟
قال:
«من أحسن في الإسلام لم يؤاخذ بما عمل في الجاهلية، ومن أساء في الإسلام أُخذ بالأول والآخر».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٩٢١)، ومسلم (١٢٠).
والإساءة معناها هنا الكفر والشرك؛ فمن أشرك بالله وكفر به بعد إسلامه أُخذ بالجاهلية والإسلام، وإلا فلا؛ لأن الله تعالى يقول:
﴿قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ يَنْتَهُوا يُغْفَرْ لَهُمْ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾
 [الأنفال: ٣٨]
وفي حديث عمرو بن العاص الآتي:
«إن الإسلام يهدم ما كان قبله».

174 — Ibn Masʿūd may Allah be pleased with him reported:
A man asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, will we be held accountable for what we did during the pre-Islamic period?”
He replied:
“Whoever does well after embracing Islam will not be held accountable for what he did during the pre-Islamic period. But whoever does evil after embracing Islam will be held accountable for both the former and the latter.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6921) and Muslim (120).
The meaning of “does evil” here is disbelief and polytheism. Thus, whoever returns to associating partners with Allah and disbelieving in Him after embracing Islam will be held accountable for what he did both before and after Islam. Otherwise, he will not.
Allah Most High says:
“Say to those who disbelieve that if they cease, what has previously occurred will be forgiven for them.”
 [Sūrat al-Anfāl 8:38]
And in the following ḥadīth of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ:
“Islam erases what came before it.”

arabic_source:
١٧٥ — عن ابن شماسة المهري قال:
حضرنا عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنه وهو في سياقة الموت، فبكى طويلاً وحول وجهه إلى الجدار.
فجعل ابنه يقول:
يا أبتاه، أما بشرك رسول الله ﷺ بكذا؟ أما بشرك رسول الله ﷺ بكذا؟
قال:
فأقبل بوجهه فقال:
إن أفضل ما نعد شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، وأن محمداً رسول الله.
إني قد كنت على أطباق ثلاث:
لقد رأيتني وما أحد أشد بغضاً لرسول الله ﷺ مني، ولا أحب إلي أن أكون قد استمكنت منه فقتلته. فلو مت على تلك الحال لكنت من أهل النار.
فلما جعل الله الإسلام في قلبي أتيت النبي ﷺ فقلت:
ابسط يمينك فلأبايعك.
فبسط يمينه.
قال:
فقبضت يدي.
فقال:
«ما لك يا عمرو؟»
قلت:
أردت أن أشترط.
قال:
«تشترط بماذا؟»
قلت:
أن يُغفر لي.
قال:
«أما علمت أن الإسلام يهدم ما كان قبله، وأن الهجرة تهدم ما كان قبلها، وأن الحج يهدم ما كان قبله؟»
وما كان أحد أحب إلي من رسول الله ﷺ، ولا أجل في عيني منه. وما كنت أطيق أن أملأ عيني منه إجلالاً له، ولو سئلت أن أصفه ما أطقت؛ لأني لم أكن أملأ عيني منه.
ولو مت على تلك الحال لرجوت أن أكون من أهل الجنة.
ثم ولينا أشياء ما أدري ما حالي فيها.
فإذا أنا مت فلا تصحبني نائحة ولا نار.
فإذا دفنتموني فشنوا علي التراب شناً، ثم أقيموا حول قبري قدر ما تنحر جزور ويقسم لحمها، حتى أستأنس بكم، وأنظر ماذا أراجع به رسل ربي.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢١).
وقوله: «كنت على أطباق ثلاث»؛ أي: أحوال ومنازل، ومنه قول الله تعالى:
﴿لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَنْ طَبَقٍ﴾
 [الانشقاق: ١٩]
أي: حالاً بعد حال.
وقوله: «فشنوا علي التراب شناً»؛ روي بالسين المهملة والمعجمة. فقيل: هما بمعنى واحد، وهو الصب. وقيل: بالمهملة الصب في سهولة، وبالمعجمة الصب في تفريق.
وهذه سنة في صب التراب على الميت في القبر. قاله عياض.
المفهم للقرطبي (١/٣٣٠).

175 — Ibn Shumāsah al-Mahrī reported:
We were present with ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ may Allah be pleased with him while he was in the throes of death. He wept for a long time and turned his face toward the wall.
His son began saying:
“Father, did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not give you glad tidings of such-and-such? Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not give you glad tidings of such-and-such?”
ʿAmr turned toward them and said:
“The best thing we have prepared is the testimony that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah.
I passed through three different stages.
I remember a time when no one was more hateful to me than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and there was nothing I desired more than to gain power over him and kill him. Had I died in that state, I would certainly have been among the people of the Fire.
Then when Allah placed Islam within my heart, I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
‘Extend your right hand so that I may pledge allegiance to you.’
He extended his right hand, but I drew my hand back.
He asked:
‘What is the matter with you, O ʿAmr?’
I replied:
‘I wish to stipulate a condition.’
He asked:
‘What condition do you wish to stipulate?’
I replied:
‘That I be forgiven.’
He said:
‘Do you not know that Islam erases what came before it, that migration erases what came before it, and that ḥajj erases what came before it?’
Thereafter, no one was more beloved to me than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor was anyone greater in my eyes than he was.
I could not fill my eyes with looking at him because of my reverence for him. If I were asked to describe him, I would be unable to do so because I never gazed fully at him.
Had I died in that state, I would have hoped to be among the people of Paradise.
Then we were entrusted with various affairs, and I do not know what my condition in them has been.
When I die, let no wailing woman accompany me and let no fire accompany me.
When you bury me, pour the earth over me, then remain around my grave for the length of time it takes to slaughter a camel and distribute its meat, so that I may feel comforted by your presence and consider how I should answer the messengers of my Lord.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (121).
His words, “I passed through three stages,” mean three successive conditions and phases, as in the words of Allah Most High:
“You will surely pass from one stage to another.”
 [Sūrat al-Inshiqāq 84:19]
That is: from one condition to another.
His words, “pour the earth over me,” have been narrated with two closely related Arabic pronunciations. It has been said that both carry the meaning of pouring. It has also been said that one refers to pouring gently, while the other refers to scattering it.
ʿIyāḍ stated that this describes the practice of pouring soil over the deceased in the grave.
Al-Qurṭubī, al-Mufhim (1/330).

١٧٦ — عن حكيم بن حزام رضي الله عنه قال:
قلت:
يا رسول الله، أرأيت أشياء كنت أتحنث بها في الجاهلية من صدقة أو عتاقة وصلة رحم، فهل فيها من أجر؟
فقال النبي ﷺ:
«أسلمت على ما سلف من خير».
وفي رواية:
أن حكيم بن حزام أعتق في الجاهلية مائة رقبة، وحمل على مائة بعير، ثم أعتق في الإسلام مائة رقبة، وحمل على مائة بعير، ثم أتى النبي ﷺ فذكر نحو حديثه.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٤٣٦)، ومسلم (١٢٣).
وفي رواية قال:
«فوالله لا أدع شيئاً صنعته في الجاهلية إلا فعلت في الإسلام مثله».
وقوله: «التحنث»؛ التعبد.
وقوله: «أسلمت على ما أسلفت من خير»؛ ذهب أكثر أهل العلم إلى تأويله.
وقال الحربي:
«ما تقدم لك من الخير الذي عملته هو لك، كما تقول: أسلمت على ألف درهم، أي: على أن أحرزها لنفسه».
قال القرطبي:
«وهذا الذي قاله الحربي هو أشبهها وأولاها».

176 — Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām may Allah be pleased with him reported:
I asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what about the things I used to perform as acts of devotion during the pre-Islamic period — such as charity, freeing slaves, and maintaining ties of kinship? Is there any reward for them?”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“You embraced Islam upon the good that you had already sent forth.”
In another narration:
Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām had freed one hundred slaves during the pre-Islamic period and provided one hundred camels. Then, after embracing Islam, he freed another one hundred slaves and provided another one hundred camels. He then came to the Prophet ﷺ and related the matter as in the narration above.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1436) and Muslim (123).
In another narration he said:
“By Allah, I will not leave any good deed that I used to perform during the pre-Islamic period except that I will perform its equivalent in Islam.”
The word «التحنث» means worship and devotional practice.
Regarding the words:
“You embraced Islam upon the good that you had already sent forth,”
most scholars interpreted their meaning.
Al-Ḥarbī said:
“The good deeds you previously performed remain for you, just as one might say, ‘He embraced Islam while possessing one thousand dirhams,’ meaning that he retained them for himself.”
Al-Qurṭubī said:
“What al-Ḥarbī stated is the interpretation that most closely resembles the wording and is the most appropriate.”

١٧٧ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«إذا أسلم العبد فحسن إسلامه، كتب الله له كل حسنة كان أزلفها، ومحيت عنه كل سيئة كان أزلفها، ثم كان بعد ذلك القصاص: الحسنة بعشر أمثالها إلى سبعمائة ضعف، والسيئة بمثلها إلا أن يتجاوز الله عز وجل عنها».
صحيح: رواه النسائي (٤٩٩٨)، والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان (٢٤).
وذكره البخاري في الإيمان (٤١) معلقاً عن مالك، ولم يسنده في موضع آخر، إلا أنه أسقط قوله:
«كتب الله له كل حسنة كان أزلفها».
لأنه مشكل على القواعد؛ لأن الكافر لا يثاب على العمل الصالح الصادر منه في كفره وشركه، لأن من شرط المتقرب أن يكون عارفاً لمن يتقرب إليه، والكافر ليس كذلك.
ذكره المازري وغيره، وتابعه القاضي عياض على تقرير هذا الإشكال.
ورده النووي فقال:
الصواب الذي عليه المحققون — بل نقل بعضهم فيه الإجماع — أن الكافر إذا فعل أفعالاً جميلة كالصدقة وصلة الرحم، ثم أسلم ومات على الإسلام، أن ثواب ذلك يكتب له.
وذكر الحافظ ابن حجر في فتح الباري (١/٩٩) احتمالات أخرى، ومن أقواها قوله:
«والحق أنه لا يلزم من كتابة الثواب للمسلم في حال إسلامه تفضلاً من الله وإحساناً أن يكون ذلك لكون عمله الصادر منه في الكفر مقبولاً، والحديث إنما تضمن كتابة الثواب ولم يتعرض للقبول، ويحتمل أن يكون القبول يصير معلقاً على إسلامه، فيقبل ويثاب إن أسلم وإلا فلا».
قلت:
وعليه يدل حديث حكيم بن حزام قبله.
وقوله: «أزلفها»؛ أي: أسلفها وقدمها.

177 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When a servant embraces Islam and perfects his Islam, Allah records for him every good deed that he had previously sent forth and erases from him every bad deed that he had previously sent forth.
After that comes recompense: a good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, while a bad deed is recorded as only one like it, unless Allah, Mighty and Majestic, pardons it.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (4998) and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān (24).
Al-Bukhārī mentioned it in the Book of Faith (41) as a suspended narration from Mālik and did not provide its connected chain elsewhere. However, he omitted the words:
“Allah records for him every good deed that he had previously sent forth.”
The reason this wording was considered difficult according to certain general principles is that a disbeliever is not ordinarily rewarded for righteous deeds performed while in disbelief and polytheism, since an act of drawing near requires recognition of the One to whom the person draws near.
Al-Māzarī and others discussed this difficulty, and al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ likewise presented it.
Al-Nawawī responded:
“The correct view held by the verifying scholars — and some have even transmitted consensus upon it — is that if a disbeliever performs virtuous deeds such as giving charity and maintaining ties of kinship, then embraces Islam and dies upon Islam, the reward of those deeds is recorded for him.”
Al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar mentioned several other possibilities in Fatḥ al-Bārī (1/99). Among the strongest is his statement:
“The correct position is that Allah’s graciously recording reward for a Muslim after his Islam does not necessarily mean that the deed he performed while in disbelief had already been accepted at that time. The ḥadīth speaks only of recording the reward and does not explicitly state acceptance. It is possible that acceptance was made conditional upon his later Islam: if he embraces Islam, the deed is accepted and rewarded; otherwise, it is not.”
The preceding ḥadīth of Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām supports this interpretation.
The expression «أزلفها» means: he sent it forth and put it forward.

١٨٢ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه قال:
سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«إن الإيمان بدأ غريباً، وسيعود غريباً كما بدأ، فطوبى يومئذ للغرباء إذا فسد الناس. والذي نفس أبي القاسم بيده، ليأرز الإيمان بين هذين المسجدين كما تأرز الحية في جحرها».
حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (١٦٠٤)، وأبو يعلى (٧٥٦)، والبزار في البحر الزخار (١١١٩).
والمسجدان هما مسجد مكة، والمدينة.

182 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ may Allah be pleased with him reported:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Faith began as something strange, and it will return to being strange just as it began. So glad tidings on that day are for the strangers when the people become corrupt. By the One in whose Hand is the soul of Abū al-Qāsim, faith will retreat between these two mosques just as a snake retreats into its hole.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Imām Aḥmad (1604), Abū Yaʿlā (756), and al-Bazzār in al-Baḥr al-Zakhkhār (1119).
The two mosques are the mosque of Makkah and the mosque of Madinah.

١٨٤ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما قال:
قال رسول الله ﷺ ذات يوم ونحن عنده:
«طوبى للغرباء».
فقيل:
ومن الغرباء يا رسول الله؟
قال:
«أناس صالحون في أناس سوء كثير، من يعصيهم أكثر ممن يطيعهم».
ثم ذكر فقراء المهاجرين الذين تتقى بهم المكاره…
حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (٦٦٥٠)، وعبد الله بن المبارك في الزهد (٧٧٥)، والبيهقي في الزهد (٢٠٣).

184 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ may Allah be pleased with them reported:
One day, while we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said:
“Glad tidings are for the strangers.”
It was asked:
“Who are the strangers, O Messenger of Allah?”
He replied:
“Righteous people among a great number of corrupt people; those who disobey them are more numerous than those who obey them.”

١٨٥ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«نحن أحق بالشك من إبراهيم إذ قال:
﴿رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيْفَ تُحْيِي الْمَوْتَى قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ قَالَ بَلَى وَلَكِنْ لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾
 [البقرة: ٢٦٠]
ويرحم الله لوطاً، لقد كان يأوي إلى ركن شديد، ولو لبثت في السجن طول ما لبث يوسف لأجبت الداعي».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٧٢)، ومسلم (٢٣٧٠: ١٥٢).
قال أبو سليمان الخطابي:
ليس في قول النبي ﷺ:
«نحن أحق بالشك من إبراهيم»
اعتراف بالشك على نفسه ولا على إبراهيم، لكن فيه نفي الشك عنهما. يقول: إذا لم أشك أنا ولم أرتب في قدرة الله عز وجل على إحياء الموتى، فإبراهيم أولى بأن لا يشك ولا يرتاب.
وقال ذلك على سبيل التواضع والهضم من النفس.
وفيه الإعلام أن المسألة من قِبَل إبراهيم لم تعرض من جهة الشك، لكن من قِبَل زيادة العلم؛ فإن العيان يفيد من المعرفة والطمأنينة ما لا يفيد الاستدلال.
وقوله:
﴿لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾
أي: بيقين النظر.
انتهى باختصار. انظر: أعلام الحديث (٣/١٥٤٥–١٥٤٦).
وقوله:
«لأجبت الداعي»
أي: لأسرعت الإجابة في الخروج من السجن، ولما قدمت طلب البراءة. فوصف يوسف عليه السلام بشدة الصبر حيث لم يبادر بالخروج.
وإنما قاله النبي ﷺ تواضعاً، والتواضع لا يحط مرتبة الكبير، بل يزيده رفعة وجلالاً.
وقيل: هو من جنس قول النبي ﷺ:
«لا تفضلوني على يونس».
انظر: فتح الباري (٦/٤١٣).

185 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“We have more right to doubt than Ibrāhīm, when he said:
‘My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.’ He said, ‘Do you not believe?’ He replied, ‘Yes, but so that my heart may be reassured.’
 [Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:260]
May Allah have mercy upon Lūṭ; indeed, he used to seek refuge in a strong support. And if I had remained in prison for as long as Yūsuf remained, I would have answered the caller.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3372) and Muslim (2370:152).
Abū Sulaymān al-Khaṭṭābī said:
The Prophet’s statement:
“We have more right to doubt than Ibrāhīm”
is not an admission of doubt either on his own part or on the part of Ibrāhīm. Rather, it negates doubt from both of them. Its meaning is: if I do not doubt or waver concerning Allah’s power, Mighty and Majestic, to bring the dead to life, then Ibrāhīm is even more deserving of not doubting or wavering.
The Prophet ﷺ said this out of humility and self-effacement.
It also clarifies that Ibrāhīm’s request did not arise from doubt, but from seeking an increase in knowledge, for direct observation gives a degree of knowledge and reassurance beyond that obtained through inference alone.
His words:
“So that my heart may be reassured”
mean: through the certainty produced by direct observation.
This is abridged. See Aʿlām al-Ḥadīth (3/1545–1546).
The Prophet’s statement:
“I would have answered the caller”
means: I would have hastened to respond and leave the prison rather than first requesting formal vindication. Yūsuf peace be upon him was thus described as possessing tremendous patience because he did not hasten to leave.
The Prophet ﷺ said this by way of humility. Humility does not diminish the rank of a great person; rather, it increases him in elevation and dignity.
It has also been said that this is similar to his statement:
“Do not prefer me over Yūnus.”
See Fatḥ al-Bārī (6/413).

١٨٦ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«لا تقوم الساعة حتى تطلع الشمس من مغربها، فإذا طلعت ورآها الناس آمن من عليها، فذاك حين:
﴿لَا يَنْفَعُ نَفْسًا إِيمَانُهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ آمَنَتْ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾»
 [الأنعام: ١٥٨]
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٦٣٥)، ومسلم (١٥٧).
ورواه البخاري (٤٦٣٦)، ومسلم بلفظ:
«فإذا طلعت من مغربها آمن الناس كلهم أجمعون، فيومئذ:
﴿لَا يَنْفَعُ نَفْسًا إِيمَانُهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ آمَنَتْ مِنْ قَبْلُ أَوْ كَسَبَتْ فِي إِيمَانِهَا خَيْرًا﴾»
 [الأنعام: ١٥٨]
english_source:
186 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The Hour will not be established until the sun rises from the west. When it rises and the people see it, everyone upon the earth will believe. That will be the time when:
‘No soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before.’”
 [Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:158]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4635) and Muslim (157).
Al-Bukhārī (4636) and Muslim also narrated:
“When it rises from the west, all the people will believe altogether. On that day:
‘No soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned any good through its faith.’”
 [Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:158]

١٨٨ — عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه، أن النبي ﷺ قال يوماً:
«أتدرون أين تذهب هذه الشمس؟»
قالوا:
الله ورسوله أعلم.
قال:
«إن هذه تجري حتى تنتهي إلى مستقرها تحت العرش، فتخر ساجدة، فلا تزال كذلك حتى يقال لها: ارتفعي، ارجعي من حيث جئت، فترجع، فتصبح طالعة من مطلعها.
ثم تجري حتى تنتهي إلى مستقرها تحت العرش، فتخر ساجدة، ولا تزال كذلك حتى يقال لها: ارتفعي، ارجعي من حيث جئت، فترجع، فتصبح طالعة من مطلعها.
ثم تجري لا يستنكر الناس منها شيئاً، حتى تنتهي إلى مستقرها ذاك تحت العرش، فيقال لها: ارتفعي، أصبحي طالعة من مغربك، فتصبح طالعة من مغربها».
فقال رسول الله ﷺ:
«أتدرون متى ذاكم؟ ذاك حين:
﴿لَا يَنْفَعُ نَفْسًا إِيمَانُهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ آمَنَتْ مِنْ قَبْلُ أَوْ كَسَبَتْ فِي إِيمَانِهَا خَيْرًا﴾»
 [الأنعام: ١٥٨]
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣١٩٩)، ومسلم (١٥٩)، واللفظ لمسلم.
وفي رواية لهما:
«فذلك قوله تعالى:
﴿وَالشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَهَا ذَلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ﴾»
 [يس: ٣٨]

english_source:
188 — Abū Dharr may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said one day:
“Do you know where this sun goes?”
They replied:
“Allah and His Messenger know best.”
He said:
“It travels until it reaches its resting place beneath the Throne. It then falls down in prostration and remains that way until it is said to it:
‘Rise and return from where you came.’
It returns and rises from its usual place of rising.
Then it travels until it reaches its resting place beneath the Throne, falls in prostration, and remains that way until it is said to it:
‘Rise and return from where you came.’
It returns and rises from its usual place of rising.
Then it continues traveling, while the people notice nothing unusual about it, until it reaches that resting place beneath the Throne. Then it will be said to it:
‘Rise and emerge from your place of setting.’
So it will rise from the west.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said:
“Do you know when that will occur? It will be when:
‘No soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned any good through its faith.’”
 [Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:158]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3199) and Muslim (159), with the wording of Muslim.
In another narration found in both collections:
“That is the meaning of Allah’s statement:
‘And the sun runs to its resting place. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.’”
 [Sūrat Yā Sīn 36:38]

١٨٩ — عن المعرور قال:
لقيت أبا ذر رضي الله عنه بالربذة، وعليه حلة، وعلى غلامه حلة.
فسألته عن ذلك فقال:
إني ساببت رجلاً فعيّرته بأمه، فقال النبي ﷺ:

وقوله:
«عيّرته بأمه»
أي: أن أمه كانت أعجمية.

189 — Al-Maʿrūr reported:
I met Abū Dharr may Allah be pleased with him at al-Rabadhah. He was wearing a set of clothing, and his servant was wearing a similar set.
I asked him about this, and he said:
“I once exchanged insults with a man and reproached him concerning his mother. The Prophet ﷺ said to me:
‘O Abū Dharr, did you reproach him concerning his mother? You are a man in whom there remains a trait of Jāhiliyyah. Your servants are your brothers whom Allah has placed under your authority. Whoever has his brother under his authority should feed him from what he himself eats, clothe him from what he himself wears, and not burden him with work beyond his ability. If you do burden him, then help him.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (30) and Muslim (1661).
The words:
“You reproached him concerning his mother”
refer to the fact that the man’s mother was non-Arab.

١٩٠ — عن أبي أمامة رضي الله عنه قال:
سأل رجل النبي ﷺ فقال:
ما الإثم؟
فقال:
«إذا حك في نفسك شيء فدعه».
قال:
فما الإيمان؟
قال:
«إذا ساءتك سيئتك، وسرتك حسنتك، فأنت مؤمن».
صحيح: رواه الإمام أحمد (٢٢١٥٩)، والطبراني (٧٥٣٩)، وصححه ابن حبان (١٧٦).

190 — Abū Umāmah may Allah be pleased with him reported:
A man asked the Prophet ﷺ:
“What is sin?”
He replied:
“When something troubles you inwardly, then leave it.”
The man asked:
“What is faith?”
He replied:
“When your bad deed saddens you and your good deed pleases you, then you are a believer.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Imām Aḥmad (22159) and al-Ṭabarānī (7539), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (176).

١٩١ — عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال:
خطبنا عمر رضي الله عنه بالجابية فقال:
يا أيها الناس، إني قمت فيكم كمقام رسول الله ﷺ فينا، فقال:
«أوصيكم بأصحابي، ثم الذين يلونهم، ثم الذين يلونهم. ثم يفشو الكذب حتى يحلف الرجل ولا يستحلف، ويشهد الشاهد ولا يستشهد.
ألا لا يخلون رجل بامرأة إلا كان ثالثهما الشيطان.
عليكم بالجماعة، وإياكم والفرقة؛ فإن الشيطان مع الواحد، وهو من الاثنين أبعد.
من أراد بحبوحة الجنة فليلزم الجماعة.
من سرته حسنته وساءته سيئته فذلكم المؤمن».
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٢١٦٥)، وأحمد (١١٤)، وصححه ابن حبان (٧٢٥٤).

191 — Ibn ʿUmar may Allah be pleased with them reported:
ʿUmar may Allah be pleased with him delivered a sermon to us at al-Jābiyah and said:
“O people, I have stood among you just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ once stood among us, and he said:
‘I instruct you to hold fast to my Companions, then those who come after them, then those who come after them.
Then lying will become widespread, until a man will swear an oath without being asked to swear, and a witness will testify without being asked to testify.
Indeed, no man should be alone with a woman, for Satan will be the third of them.
You must remain with the united community, and beware of division, for Satan is with one person and is farther away from two.
Whoever desires the central and spacious part of Paradise should adhere to the united community.
Whoever is pleased by his good deed and saddened by his bad deed — that person is the believer.’”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2165) and Aḥmad (114), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (7254).

arabic_source:
١٩٢ — عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«إن من الشجر شجرة لا يسقط ورقها، وإنها مثل المسلم، فحدثوني ما هي؟»
فوقع الناس في شجر البوادي.
قال عبد الله بن عمر:
ووقع في نفسي أنها النخلة، فاستحييت.
ثم قالوا:
حدثنا ما هي يا رسول الله؟
قال:
«هي النخلة».
وفي رواية:
«أخبروني شجرة مثلها مثل المسلم، تؤتي أكلها كل حين بإذن ربها، ولا تحات ورقها».
فوقع في نفسي النخلة، فكرهت أن أتكلم وثم أبو بكر وعمر.
فلما لم يتكلما قال النبي ﷺ:
«هي النخلة».
فلما خرجت مع أبي قلت:
يا أبتاه، وقع في نفسي النخلة.
قال:
ما منعك أن تقولها؟ لو كنت قلتها كان أحب إلي من كذا وكذا.
قال:
ما منعني إلا أني لم أرك ولا أبا بكر تكلمتما، فكرهت.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦١)، ومسلم (٢٨١١). والرواية الثانية عند البخاري (٦١٤٤).

192 — Ibn ʿUmar may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Among the trees there is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it resembles the Muslim. Tell me which tree it is.”
The people began thinking of the trees of the desert.
ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said:
It occurred to me that it was the date palm, but I felt shy to speak.
They then asked:
“Tell us which tree it is, O Messenger of Allah.”
He replied:
“It is the date palm.”
In another narration:
“Tell me of a tree whose likeness is that of the Muslim: it gives its fruit at all times by the permission of its Lord, and its leaves do not fall.”
It occurred to me that it was the date palm, but I disliked speaking while Abū Bakr and ʿUmar were present.
When neither of them spoke, the Prophet ﷺ said:
“It is the date palm.”
When I later went out with my father, I said:
“Father, it occurred to me that it was the date palm.”
He replied:

أرأيت إن لقيت رجلاً من الكفار فاقتتلنا، فضرب إحدى يدي بالسيف فقطعها، ثم لاذ مني بشجرة فقال:
أسلمت لله.
أأقتله يا رسول الله بعد أن قالها؟
فقال رسول الله ﷺ:
«لا تقتله».

«لا تقتله، فإن قتلته فإنه بمنزلتك قبل أن تقتله، وإنك بمنزلته قبل أن يقول كلمته التي قال».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٠١٩)، ومسلم (٩٥).

193 — ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Khiyār reported that al-Miqdād ibn ʿAmr al-Kindī may Allah be pleased with him — an ally of Banū Zuhrah and one of those who participated in Badr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
“Suppose I encounter a man from among the disbelievers and we fight. He strikes one of my hands with his sword and cuts it off, then takes refuge from me behind a tree and says:
‘I have submitted to Allah.’
May I kill him, O Messenger of Allah, after he has said that?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“Do not kill him.”
He said:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Do not kill him. If you kill him, he will be in the position you were in before you killed him, and you will be in the position he was in before he uttered the statement that he said.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4019) and Muslim (95).

١٩٤ — عن أسامة بن زيد رضي الله عنهما قال:
بعثنا رسول الله ﷺ إلى الحرقة، فصبحنا القوم فهزمناهم، ولحقت أنا ورجل من الأنصار رجلاً منهم.
فلما غشيناه قال:
لا إله إلا الله.
فكف عنه الأنصاري، فطعنته برمحي حتى قتلته.
فلما قدمنا بلغ ذلك النبي ﷺ فقال:
«يا أسامة، أقتلته بعد ما قال لا إله إلا الله؟»
قلت:
كان متعوذاً!
فما زال يكررها حتى تمنيت أني لم أكن أسلمت قبل ذلك اليوم.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٢٦٩)، ومسلم (٩٦: ١٥٩).
ورواه مسلم من وجه آخر، عن أسامة بن زيد رضي الله عنهما قال:
بعثنا رسول الله ﷺ في سرية، فصبحنا الحرقات من جهينة، فأدركت رجلاً فقال:
لا إله إلا الله.
فطعنته.
فوقع في نفسي من ذلك، فذكرته للنبي ﷺ.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ:
«أقال لا إله إلا الله وقتلته؟!»
قلت:
يا رسول الله، إنما قالها خوفاً من السلاح.
قال:
«أفلا شققت عن قلبه حتى تعلم أقالها أم لا؟!»
فما زال يكررها علي حتى تمنيت أني أسلمت يومئذ.
قال:
فقال سعد:
وأنا والله لا أقتل مسلماً حتى يقتله ذو البطين — يعني أسامة.
قال:
فقال رجل:
ألم يقل الله:
﴿وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّى لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ كُلُّهُ لِلَّهِ﴾
 [الأنفال: ٣٩]
فقال سعد:
قد قاتلنا حتى لا تكون فتنة، وأنت وأصحابك تريدون أن تقاتلوا حتى تكون فتنة.
وقوله: «الحرقات» مثل عرفات وأذرعات، موضع ببلاد جهينة.

194 — Usāmah ibn Zayd may Allah be pleased with them reported:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us against al-Ḥuraqah. We attacked the people at dawn and defeated them.
A man from the Anṣār and I caught up with one of them. When we overtook him, he said:
“There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.”
The Anṣārī man held back from him, but I stabbed him with my spear until I killed him.
When we returned, news of this reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
“O Usāmah, did you kill him after he said, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah’?”
I replied:
“He only said it to seek protection!”
The Prophet ﷺ continued repeating the question until I wished that I had not embraced Islam before that day.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4269) and Muslim (96:159).
Muslim also narrated through another route from Usāmah ibn Zayd may Allah be pleased with them:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us on an expedition. We attacked al-Ḥuraqāt of Juhaynah at dawn.
I caught up with a man who said:
“There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.”
But I stabbed him.
The matter troubled me, so I mentioned it to the Prophet ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“He said, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah,’ and you killed him?!”
I replied:
“O Messenger of Allah, he only said it out of fear of the weapon.”
He said:
“Why did you not split open his heart so that you could know whether he said it or not?!”
He continued repeating this to me until I wished that I had only embraced Islam on that very day.
Saʿd said:
“By Allah, I will not kill a Muslim until the man with the broad belly kills him” — meaning Usāmah.
A man asked:
“Did Allah not say:
‘Fight them until there is no persecution and religion is entirely for Allah’?”
 [Sūrat al-Anfāl 8:39]
Saʿd replied:
“We fought until there was no persecution, whereas you and your companions wish to fight until there is persecution.”
The name «الحرقات» is formed like ʿArafāt and Adhruʿāt and refers to a place in the territory of Juhaynah.

١٩٥ — عن جندب بن عبد الله البجلي رضي الله عنه:
أنه بعث إلى عسعس بن سلامة زمن فتنة ابن الزبير، فقال:
اجمع لي نفراً من إخوانك حتى أحدثهم.
فبعث رسولاً إليهم.
فلما اجتمعوا جاء جندب وعليه برنس أصفر فقال:
تحدثوا بما كنتم تحدثون به حتى دار الحديث.
فلما دار الحديث إليه حسر البرنس عن رأسه فقال:
إني أتيتكم ولا أريد أن أخبركم عن نبيكم.
إن رسول الله ﷺ بعث بعثاً من المسلمين إلى قوم من المشركين، وأنهم التقوا.
فكان رجل من المشركين إذا شاء أن يقصد إلى رجل من المسلمين قصد له فقتله.
وإن رجلاً من المسلمين قصد غفلته — قال: وكنا نحدث أنه أسامة بن زيد — فلما رفع عليه السيف قال:
لا إله إلا الله.
فقتله!
فجاء البشير إلى النبي ﷺ فسأله، فأخبره حتى أخبره خبر الرجل كيف صنع.
فدعاه فسأله فقال:
«لم قتلته؟»
قال:
يا رسول الله، أوجع في المسلمين، وقتل فلاناً وفلاناً — وسمى له نفراً — وإني حملت عليه، فلما رأى السيف قال:
لا إله إلا الله.
قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«أقتلته؟»
قال:
نعم.
قال:
«فكيف تصنع بلا إله إلا الله إذا جاءت يوم القيامة؟»
قال:
يا رسول الله، استغفر لي.
قال:
«وكيف تصنع بلا إله إلا الله إذا جاءت يوم القيامة؟!»
فجعل لا يزيده على أن يقول:
«كيف تصنع بلا إله إلا الله إذا جاءت يوم القيامة؟!»
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٩٧).

195 — Jundub ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Bajalī may Allah be pleased with him sent for ʿAsʿas ibn Salāmah during the turmoil of Ibn al-Zubayr and said:
“Gather a group of your brothers for me so that I may speak to them.”
He sent for them, and when they had gathered, Jundub came wearing a yellow hooded cloak.
He said:
“Continue speaking about what you were discussing until the conversation comes around.”
When the discussion reached him, he uncovered his head and said:
“I have come to you, and I intend to narrate to you from your Prophet.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a detachment of Muslims against a group of polytheists, and the two sides met.
There was a man among the polytheists who, whenever he targeted a Muslim, would attack and kill him.
Then one of the Muslims waited for an opportunity to attack him — and we used to say that this Muslim was Usāmah ibn Zayd.
When he raised his sword over the man, the man said:
‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.’
But he killed him.
When the bearer of good news returned to the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet asked him about what had happened. He informed him of the man’s story and what he had done.
The Prophet ﷺ called him and asked:
‘Why did you kill him?’
He replied:
‘O Messenger of Allah, he had severely harmed the Muslims and killed so-and-so and so-and-so,’ and he named several people. ‘I attacked him, and when he saw the sword he said: “There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.”’
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
‘Did you kill him?’
He replied:
‘Yes.’
The Prophet ﷺ said:
‘Then what will you do with “There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah” when it comes on the Day of Resurrection?’
He said:
‘O Messenger of Allah, seek forgiveness for me.’
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
‘And what will you do with “There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah” when it comes on the Day of Resurrection?!’
He continued saying nothing to him except:
‘What will you do with “There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah” when it comes on the Day of Resurrection?!’”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (97).

فكان رجل من المشركين إذا شاء أن يقصد إلى رجل من المسلمين قصد له فقتله.
وإن رجلاً من المسلمين قصد غفلته — قال: وكنا نحدث أنه أسامة بن زيد — فلما رفع عليه السيف قال:
لا إله إلا الله.
فقتله!
فجاء البشير إلى النبي ﷺ فسأله، فأخبره حتى أخبره خبر الرجل كيف صنع.
فدعاه فسأله فقال:
«لم قتلته؟»
قال:
يا رسول الله، أوجع في المسلمين، وقتل فلاناً وفلاناً — وسمى له نفراً — وإني حملت عليه، فلما رأى السيف قال:
لا إله إلا الله.
قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«أقتلته؟»
قال:
نعم.
قال:
«فكيف تصنع بلا إله إلا الله إذا جاءت يوم القيامة؟»
قال:
يا رسول الله، استغفر لي.
قال:
«وكيف تصنع بلا إله إلا الله إذا جاءت يوم القيامة؟!»
فجعل لا يزيده على أن يقول:
«كيف تصنع بلا إله إلا الله إذا جاءت يوم القيامة؟!»
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٩٧).
195 — Jundub ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Bajalī may Allah be pleased with him sent for ʿAsʿas ibn Salāmah during the turmoil of Ibn al-Zubayr and said:
“Gather a group of your brothers for me so that I may speak to them.”
He sent for them, and when they had gathered, Jundub came wearing a yellow hooded cloak.
He said:
“Continue speaking about what you were discussing until the conversation comes around.”
When the discussion reached him, he uncovered his head and said:
“I have come to you, and I intend to narrate to you from your Prophet.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a detachment of Muslims against a group of polytheists, and the two sides met.
There was a man among the polytheists who, whenever he targeted a Muslim, would attack and kill him.
Then one of the Muslims waited for an opportunity to attack him — and we used to say that this Muslim was Usāmah ibn Zayd.
When he raised his sword over the man, the man said:
‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.’
But he killed him.
When the bearer of good news returned to the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet asked him about what had happened. He informed him of the man’s story and what he had done.
The Prophet ﷺ called him and asked:
‘Why did you kill him?’
He replied:
‘O Messenger of Allah, he had severely harmed the Muslims and killed so-and-so and so-and-so,’ and he named several people. ‘I attacked him, and when he saw the sword he said: “There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.”’
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
‘Did you kill him?’
He replied:
‘Yes.’
The Prophet ﷺ said:
‘Then what will you do with “There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah” when it comes on the Day of Resurrection?’
He said:
‘O Messenger of Allah, seek forgiveness for me.’
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
‘And what will you do with “There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah” when it comes on the Day of Resurrection?!’
He continued saying nothing to him except:
‘What will you do with “There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah” when it comes on the Day of Resurrection?!’”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (97).

١٩٦ — عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«من قال لأخيه: يا كافر، فقد باء بها أحدهما».
متفق عليه: رواه مالك (١)، والبخاري (٦١٠٤)، ومسلم (٦٠).
وزاد مسلم:
«إن كان كما قال، وإلا رجعت عليه».

196 — Ibn ʿUmar may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever says to his brother, ‘O disbeliever,’ then one of the two has incurred it.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik (1), al-Bukhārī (6104), and Muslim (60).
Muslim added:
“If he is as the speaker said, then so it is; otherwise, it returns upon the one who said it.”

١٩٨ — عن ثابت بن الضحاك رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«من حلف بملة غير الإسلام كاذباً فهو كما قال، ومن قتل نفسه بشيء عذب به في نار جهنم، ولعن المؤمن كقتله، ومن رمى مؤمناً بكفر فهو كقتله».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦١٠٥)، ومسلم (١١٠)، واللفظ للبخاري.

198 — Thābit ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever falsely swears by a religion other than Islam is as he has said. Whoever kills himself with something will be punished with it in the Fire of Hell. Cursing a believer is like killing him, and whoever accuses a believer of disbelief is like killing him.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6105) and Muslim (110), with the wording of al-Bukhārī.

Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4687).

٢٠١ — عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه، أنه سمع النبي ﷺ يقول:
«ليس من رجل ادعى لغير أبيه — وهو يعلمه — إلا كفر، ومن ادعى قوماً ليس له فيهم فليتبوأ مقعده من النار».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٥٠٨)، ومسلم (٦١).
وزاد مسلم:
«ومن دعا رجلاً بالكفر، أو قال: عدو الله، وليس كذلك، إلا حار عليه».
وقوله: «حار عليه»؛ أي: باء ورجع.

201 — Abū Dharr may Allah be pleased with him reported that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
“No man knowingly claims someone other than his true father except that he has committed disbelief. And whoever claims to belong to a people to whom he does not belong, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3508) and Muslim (61).
Muslim added:
“Whoever calls a man a disbeliever, or says to him, ‘Enemy of Allah,’ when he is not so, the accusation returns upon him.”
The expression «حار عليه» means that it returns upon him and he bears its consequence.

“Whoever calls a man a disbeliever, or says to him, ‘Enemy of Allah,’ when he is not so, the accusation returns upon him.”
The expression «حار عليه» means that it returns upon him and he bears its consequence.

٢٠٥ — عن جرير بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«أيما عبد أبق برئت منه الذمة».
وفي رواية:
«إذا أبق العبد لم تقبل له صلاة».
وفي رواية:
«أيما عبد أبق من مواليه فقد كفر حتى يرجع إليهم».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٦٩).

“Any slave who runs away has the covenant of protection disclaimed from him.”
In another narration:
“If a slave runs away, his prayer is not accepted.”
And in another narration:
“Any slave who runs away from his masters has committed an act of disbelief until he returns to them.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (69).

٢٠٦ — عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت:
سأل أناس النبي ﷺ عن الكهان، فقال:
«إنهم ليسوا بشيء».
فقالوا:
يا رسول الله، فإنهم يحدثون بالشيء يكون حقاً!
قال النبي ﷺ:
«تلك الكلمة من الحق يخطفها الجني، فيقرقرها في أذن وليه كقرقرة الدجاجة، فيخلطون فيه أكثر من مائة كذبة».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٥٦١)، ومسلم (٢٢٢٨).

206 — ʿĀʾishah may Allah be pleased with her reported:
Some people asked the Prophet ﷺ about soothsayers.
He said:
“They are nothing.”
They said:
“O Messenger of Allah, sometimes they tell us something that turns out to be true.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“That is a word of truth which a jinn snatches and pours into the ear of his ally like the clucking of a hen; then they mix with it more than one hundred lies.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7561) and Muslim (2228).

٢٠٧ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«ما من مولود إلا يولد على الفطرة، فأبواه يهودانه وينصرانه ويمجسانه، كما تنتج البهيمة بهيمة جمعاء، هل تحسون فيها من جدعاء؟»
ثم يقول أبو هريرة:
واقرؤوا إن شئتم:
﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا فِطْرَتَ اللهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللهِ ذَلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾
 [الروم: ٣٠]
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٣٥٩)، ومسلم (٢٦٥٨).

207 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“No newborn is born except upon the natural disposition. Then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete and sound offspring. Do you perceive any mutilation in it?”
Abū Hurayrah would then say:
Recite, if you wish:
“So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth — the natural disposition of Allah upon which He created mankind. There is no altering the creation of Allah. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know.”
 [Sūrat al-Rūm 30:30]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1359) and Muslim (2658).

«ما من مولود إلا يولد على الفطرة، فأبواه يهودانه وينصرانه ويمجسانه، كما تنتج البهيمة بهيمة جمعاء، هل تحسون فيها من جدعاء؟»
ثم يقول أبو هريرة:
واقرؤوا إن شئتم:
﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا فِطْرَتَ اللهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللهِ ذَلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾
 [الروم: ٣٠]
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٣٥٩)، ومسلم (٢٦٥٨).
207 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“No newborn is born except upon the natural disposition. Then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete and sound offspring. Do you perceive any mutilation in it?”
Abū Hurayrah would then say:
Recite, if you wish:
“So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth — the natural disposition of Allah upon which He created mankind. There is no altering the creation of Allah. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know.”
 [Sūrat al-Rūm 30:30]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1359) and Muslim (2658).

٢٠٨ — عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«يقول الله تعالى لأهون أهل النار عذاباً يوم القيامة: لو أن لك ما في الأرض من شيء، أكنت تفتدي به؟
فيقول: نعم.
فيقول: أردت منك أهون من هذا وأنت في صلب آدم: أن لا تشرك بي شيئاً، فأبيت إلا أن تشرك بي».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٥٥٧)، ومسلم (٢٨٠٥).
ورواه مسلم من وجه آخر، وفيه:
«قد أردت منك أهون من هذا وأنت في صلب آدم: أن لا تشرك بي — أحسبه قال: ولا أدخلك النار — فأبيت إلا الشرك».

english_source:
208 — Anas ibn Mālik may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Allah Most High will say to the person receiving the lightest punishment among the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection:
‘If you possessed everything upon the earth, would you ransom yourself with it?’
He will reply:
‘Yes.’
Allah will say:
‘I asked from you something easier than that while you were in the loins of Adam: that you not associate anything with Me, yet you refused except to associate partners with Me.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6557) and Muslim (2805).
Muslim also narrated through another route:
“I asked from you something easier than this while you were in the loins of Adam: that you not associate anything with Me” — the narrator said: I think he also said, “and then I would not admit you into the Fire” — “but you refused except to commit shirk.”

٢٠٩ — عن هشام بن حكيم رضي الله عنه:
أن رجلاً أتى النبي ﷺ فقال:
يا رسول الله، أنبتدئ الأعمال أم قضي القضاء؟
فقال رسول الله ﷺ:
«إن الله عز وجل أخذ ذرية آدم من ظهره، وأشهدهم على أنفسهم، ثم أفاض بهم في كفيه فقال: هؤلاء للجنة، وهؤلاء للنار، فأهل الجنة ميسرون لعمل أهل الجنة، وأهل النار ميسرون لعمل أهل النار».
حسن: رواه الفريابي في القدر (٢٢)، وعنه الآجري في الشريعة (٣٣٠)، وابن أبي عاصم في السنة (١٦٨).

209 — Hishām ibn Ḥakīm may Allah be pleased with him reported:
A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, are deeds something that we begin anew, or has the decree already been determined?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took the descendants of Adam from his back and made them testify concerning themselves. Then He spread them forth in His two Hands and said:
‘These are for Paradise, and these are for the Fire.’
The people of Paradise are facilitated toward the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of the Fire are facilitated toward the deeds of the people of the Fire.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Firyābī in al-Qadar (22), through him by al-Ājurrī in al-Sharīʿah (330), and by Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Sunnah (168).

٢١٠ — عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«أخذ الله الميثاق من ظهر آدم بنعمان — يعني عرفة — فأخرج من صلبه كل ذرية ذرأها، فنثرهم بين يديه كالذر، ثم كلمهم قبلاً، قال:
﴿أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ ۝ أَوْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّمَا أَشْرَكَ آبَاؤُنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ أَفَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾»
 [الأعراف: ١٧٢–١٧٣]
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٤٥٥)، وابن أبي عاصم في السنة (٢٠٢)، والبيهقي في الأسماء والصفات (٧١٤).

210 — Ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Allah took the covenant from the back of Adam at Nuʿmān — meaning ʿArafah. He brought forth from his loins every descendant whom He would create and scattered them before Him like tiny particles. Then He spoke to them directly, saying:
‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes, we testify,’ lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Indeed, we were unaware of this,’ or lest you should say, ‘It was only our forefathers who associated others with Allah before us, and we were merely descendants after them. Will You then destroy us for what the falsifiers did?’”
 [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:172–173]
Ḥasan: Narrated by Aḥmad (2455), Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Sunnah (202), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa al-Ṣifāt (714).

‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes, we testify,’ lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Indeed, we were unaware of this,’ or lest you should say, ‘It was only our forefathers who associated others with Allah before us, and we were merely descendants after them. Will You then destroy us for what the falsifiers did?’”
 [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:172–173]
Ḥasan: Narrated by Aḥmad (2455), Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Sunnah (202), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa al-Ṣifāt (714).

﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ ۝ أَوْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّمَا أَشْرَكَ آبَاؤُنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ أَفَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾
 [الأعراف: ١٧٢–١٧٣]
قال:
جمعه له يومئذ جميعاً ما هو كائن منه إلى يوم القيامة، فجعلهم أرواحاً ثم صورهم، ثم استنطقهم فتكلموا، وأخذ عليهم العهد والميثاق:
﴿وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ ۝ أَوْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّمَا أَشْرَكَ آبَاؤُنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ أَفَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾.
قال:
فإني أشهد عليكم السماوات السبع، والأرضين السبع، وأشهد عليكم أباكم آدم أن تقولوا يوم القيامة: لم نعلم بهذا.
اعلموا أن لا إله غيري، ولا رب غيري، ولا تشركوا بي شيئاً، وإني سأرسل لكم رسلاً ينذرونكم عهدي وميثاقي، وأنزل عليكم كتبي.
قالوا:
نشهد أنك ربنا وإلهنا، لا رب لنا غيرك، ولا إله لنا غيرك.
فأقروا له يومئذ بالطاعة، ورفع أباهم آدم إليهم، فرأى فيهم الغني والفقير، وحسن الصورة ودون ذلك.
فقال:
يا رب، لو سويت بين عبادك؟
قال:
«إني أحببت أن أُشكر».
ورأى فيهم الأنبياء مثل السرج عليهم النور، وخصوا بميثاق آخر من الرسالة والنبوة، فهو الذي يقول تعالى:
﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِيثَاقَهُمْ وَمِنْكَ وَمِنْ نُوحٍ وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى وَعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ وَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُمْ مِيثَاقًا غَلِيظًا﴾
 [الأحزاب: ٧]
وهو الذي يقول:
﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا فِطْرَتَ اللهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللهِ﴾
 [الروم: ٣٠]
وفي ذلك قال:
﴿هَذَا نَذِيرٌ مِنَ النُّذُرِ الْأُولَى﴾
 [النجم: ٥٦]
وفي ذلك قال:
﴿وَمَا وَجَدْنَا لِأَكْثَرِهِمْ مِنْ عَهْدٍ وَإِنْ وَجَدْنَا أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَفَاسِقِينَ﴾
 [الأعراف: ١٠٢]
حسن: رواه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره (٥/١٦١٥)، وابن جرير الطبري في تفسيره (١٠/٥٥٧).

211 — Ubayy ibn Kaʿb may Allah be pleased with him said concerning the statement of Allah Most High:
“And when your Lord brought forth from the children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes, we testify,’ lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Indeed, we were unaware of this,’ or lest you should say, ‘It was only our forefathers who associated others with Allah before us, and we were merely descendants after them. Will You then destroy us for what the falsifiers did?’”
 [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:172–173]
He said:
On that day, Allah gathered for Adam all those who would descend from him until the Day of Resurrection. He made them spirits, then gave them form, then caused them to speak, and they spoke. He took from them the covenant and the solemn pledge:
“And He made them testify concerning themselves: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes, we testify,’ lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Indeed, we were unaware of this,’ or lest you should say, ‘It was only our forefathers who associated others with Allah before us, and we were merely descendants after them. Will You then destroy us for what the falsifiers did?’”
He said:
“Indeed, I call the seven heavens and the seven earths as witnesses against you, and I call your father Adam as a witness against you, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection:
‘We did not know of this.’
Know that there is no deity other than Me and no Lord other than Me. Do not associate anything with Me. I will surely send messengers to you who will remind you of My covenant and My pledge, and I will send down My Books to you.”
They said:
“We testify that You are our Lord and our God. We have no lord other than You and no deity other than You.”
Thus, on that day they acknowledged obedience to Him.
Their father Adam was raised before them. He saw among them the rich and the poor, those of beautiful appearance and those of lesser appearance.
He asked:
“My Lord, why did You not make Your servants equal?”
Allah said:
“I desired to be thanked.”
Adam saw among them the prophets, like lamps with light upon them. They were distinguished by an additional covenant concerning messengership and prophethood.
This is what Allah Most High says:
“And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus son of Mary; and We took from them a solemn covenant.”
 [Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:7]
And it is what He says:
“So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth — the natural disposition of Allah upon which He created mankind. There is no changing the creation of Allah.”
 [Sūrat al-Rūm 30:30]
And concerning this He said:
“This is a warner from the former warners.”
 [Sūrat al-Najm 53:56]
And concerning this He said:
“We did not find in most of them any covenant; indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient.”
 [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:102]
Ḥasan: Narrated by Ibn Abī Ḥātim in his Tafsīr (5/1615) and Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī in his Tafsīr (10/557).

٢١١ — عن أُبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه، في قول الله تعالى:
﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ ۝ أَوْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّمَا أَشْرَكَ آبَاؤُنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ أَفَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾
 [الأعراف: ١٧٢–١٧٣]

جمعه له يومئذ جميعاً ما هو كائن منه إلى يوم القيامة، فجعلهم أرواحاً ثم صورهم، ثم استنطقهم فتكلموا، وأخذ عليهم العهد والميثاق:

قال:
فإني أشهد عليكم السماوات السبع، والأرضين السبع، وأشهد عليكم أباكم آدم أن تقولوا يوم القيامة: لم نعلم بهذا.
اعلموا أن لا إله غيري، ولا رب غيري، ولا تشركوا بي شيئاً، وإني سأرسل لكم رسلاً ينذرونكم عهدي وميثاقي، وأنزل عليكم كتبي.
قالوا:
نشهد أنك ربنا وإلهنا، لا رب لنا غيرك، ولا إله لنا غيرك.
فأقروا له يومئذ بالطاعة، ورفع أباهم آدم إليهم، فرأى فيهم الغني والفقير، وحسن الصورة ودون ذلك.
فقال:
يا رب، لو سويت بين عبادك؟
قال:
«إني أحببت أن أُشكر».
ورأى فيهم الأنبياء مثل السرج عليهم النور، وخصوا بميثاق آخر من الرسالة والنبوة، فهو الذي يقول تعالى:
﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِيثَاقَهُمْ وَمِنْكَ وَمِنْ نُوحٍ وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى وَعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ وَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُمْ مِيثَاقًا غَلِيظًا﴾
 [الأحزاب: ٧]
وهو الذي يقول:
﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا فِطْرَتَ اللهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللهِ﴾
 [الروم: ٣٠]
وفي ذلك قال:

٢١٢ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«يأتي الشيطان أحدكم فيقول: من خلق كذا؟ من خلق كذا؟ حتى يقول: من خلق ربك؟ فإذا بلغه فليستعذ بالله ولينته».
وفي رواية:
«فليقل: آمنت بالله».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٢٧٦)، ومسلم (١٣٤/٢١٤)، واللفظ للبخاري.
والرواية الثانية عند مسلم.
ورواه مسلم أيضاً، وفيه:
«لا يزال الناس يسألونكم عن العلم حتى يقولوا: هذا الله خلقنا، فمن خلق الله؟»
قال — وهو آخذ بيد رجل —:
صدق الله ورسوله، قد سألني اثنان وهذا الثالث.
أو قال:
سألني واحد وهذا الثاني.
وفي رواية قال:
قال لي رسول الله ﷺ:
«لا يزالون يسألونك يا أبا هريرة حتى يقولوا: هذا الله، فمن خلق الله؟»
قال أبو هريرة:
فبينما أنا في المسجد إذ جاءني ناس من الأعراب فقالوا:
يا أبا هريرة، هذا الله، فمن خلق الله؟
فأخذ حصى بكفه فرماهم، وقال:
قوموا، قوموا، صدق خليلي.
وفي رواية قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«لا يزالون يسألون حتى يقال: هذا الله خلقنا، فمن خلق الله عز وجل؟»
قال أبو هريرة:
فوالله إني لجالس يوماً إذ قال لي رجل من أهل العراق:
هذا الله خلقنا، فمن خلق الله عز وجل؟
قال أبو هريرة:
فجعلت إصبعي في أذني، ثم صحت فقلت:
صدق الله ورسوله:
﴿اللهُ أَحَدٌ ۝ اللهُ الصَّمَدُ ۝ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ۝ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ﴾.
ورواه ابن أبي عاصم في السنة (٦٥٣)، وزاد فيه:
«ثم ليتفل عن يساره، وليستعذ بالله من الشيطان».

english_source:
212 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Satan comes to one of you and asks:
‘Who created this? Who created that?’
until he says:
‘Who created your Lord?’
When he reaches that point, let him seek refuge in Allah and stop.”
In another narration:
“Let him say: ‘I believe in Allah.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3276) and Muslim (134/214), with the wording of al-Bukhārī.
The second wording is narrated by Muslim.
Muslim also narrated:
“People will continue asking you concerning knowledge until they say:
‘Allah created us, so who created Allah?’”
Abū Hurayrah said this while holding the hand of a man and then said:
“Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. Two people have already asked me this, and this is the third.”
Or he said:
“One person asked me this, and this is the second.”
In another narration, Abū Hurayrah said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
“They will continue asking you, O Abū Hurayrah, until they say:
‘This is Allah — so who created Allah?’”
Abū Hurayrah said:
While I was in the mosque, some Bedouins came to me and said:
“O Abū Hurayrah, this is Allah — so who created Allah?”
He took some pebbles in his hand and threw them toward them, saying:
“Leave! Leave! My beloved companion spoke the truth.”
In another narration, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“They will continue asking until it is said:
‘Allah created us, so who created Allah, Mighty and Majestic?’”
Abū Hurayrah said:
By Allah, one day I was sitting when a man from Iraq said to me:
“Allah created us, so who created Allah, Mighty and Majestic?”
I put my finger into my ear and cried out:
“Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth:
‘Allah is One. Allah, the Self-Sufficient. He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him.’”
Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim narrated it in al-Sunnah (653) and added:
“Then let him spit lightly to his left and seek refuge in Allah from Satan.”

٢١٢ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«يأتي الشيطان أحدكم فيقول: من خلق كذا؟ من خلق كذا؟ حتى يقول: من خلق ربك؟ فإذا بلغه فليستعذ بالله ولينته».
وفي رواية:
«فليقل: آمنت بالله».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٢٧٦)، ومسلم (١٣٤/٢١٤)، واللفظ للبخاري.
والرواية الثانية عند مسلم.
ورواه مسلم أيضاً، وفيه:
«لا يزال الناس يسألونكم عن العلم حتى يقولوا: هذا الله خلقنا، فمن خلق الله؟»
قال — وهو آخذ بيد رجل —:
صدق الله ورسوله، قد سألني اثنان وهذا الثالث.
أو قال:
سألني واحد وهذا الثاني.
وفي رواية قال:
قال لي رسول الله ﷺ:
«لا يزالون يسألونك يا أبا هريرة حتى يقولوا: هذا الله، فمن خلق الله؟»
قال أبو هريرة:
فبينما أنا في المسجد إذ جاءني ناس من الأعراب فقالوا:
يا أبا هريرة، هذا الله، فمن خلق الله؟
فأخذ حصى بكفه فرماهم، وقال:
قوموا، قوموا، صدق خليلي.
وفي رواية قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«لا يزالون يسألون حتى يقال: هذا الله خلقنا، فمن خلق الله عز وجل؟»
قال أبو هريرة:
فوالله إني لجالس يوماً إذ قال لي رجل من أهل العراق:
هذا الله خلقنا، فمن خلق الله عز وجل؟
قال أبو هريرة:
فجعلت إصبعي في أذني، ثم صحت فقلت:
صدق الله ورسوله:
﴿اللهُ أَحَدٌ ۝ اللهُ الصَّمَدُ ۝ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ۝ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ﴾.
ورواه ابن أبي عاصم في السنة (٦٥٣)، وزاد فيه:
«ثم ليتفل عن يساره، وليستعذ بالله من الشيطان».
212 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Satan comes to one of you and asks:
‘Who created this? Who created that?’
until he says:
‘Who created your Lord?’
When he reaches that point, let him seek refuge in Allah and stop.”
In another narration:
“Let him say: ‘I believe in Allah.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3276) and Muslim (134/214), with the wording of al-Bukhārī.
The second wording is narrated by Muslim.
Muslim also narrated:
“People will continue asking you concerning knowledge until they say:
‘Allah created us, so who created Allah?’”
Abū Hurayrah said this while holding the hand of a man and then said:
“Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. Two people have already asked me this, and this is the third.”
Or he said:
“One person asked me this, and this is the second.”
In another narration, Abū Hurayrah said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
“They will continue asking you, O Abū Hurayrah, until they say:
‘This is Allah — so who created Allah?’”
Abū Hurayrah said:
While I was in the mosque, some Bedouins came to me and said:
“O Abū Hurayrah, this is Allah — so who created Allah?”
He took some pebbles in his hand and threw them toward them, saying:
“Leave! Leave! My beloved companion spoke the truth.”
In another narration, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“They will continue asking until it is said:
‘Allah created us, so who created Allah, Mighty and Majestic?’”
Abū Hurayrah said:
By Allah, one day I was sitting when a man from Iraq said to me:
“Allah created us, so who created Allah, Mighty and Majestic?”
I put my finger into my ear and cried out:
“Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth:
‘Allah is One. Allah, the Self-Sufficient. He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him.’”
Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim narrated it in al-Sunnah (653) and added:
“Then let him spit lightly to his left and seek refuge in Allah from Satan.”

٢١٣ — عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«لن يبرح الناس يتساءلون حتى يقولوا: هذا الله خالق كل شيء، فمن خلق الله؟»
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٢٩٦) واللفظ له، ومسلم (١٣٦).
وفي رواية مسلم:
«قال الله عز وجل: إن أمتك لا يزالون يقولون: ما كذا؟ ما كذا؟ حتى يقولوا: هذا الله خلق الخلق، فمن خلق الله؟»

english_source:
213 — Anas ibn Mālik may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“People will not cease questioning until they say:
‘Allah is the Creator of everything, so who created Allah?’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7296), whose wording is cited here, and Muslim (136).
In Muslim’s wording:
“Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:
‘Your Ummah will continue saying: What about this? What about that? until they say: Allah created creation, so who created Allah?’”

٢١٤ — عن عائشة رضي الله عنها، أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«إن أحدكم يأتيه الشيطان فيقول: من خلقك؟
فيقول: الله.
فيقول: فمن خلق الله؟
فإذا وجد ذلك أحدكم فليقرأ: آمنت بالله ورسله، فإن ذلك يذهب عنه».
صحيح: رواه الإمام أحمد (٢٦٢٠٣)، والبزار في كشف الأستار (٥٠)، وأبو يعلى (٤٧٠٤).
وصححه ابن حبان (١٥٠)، ولفظه:
«لن يدع الشيطان أن يأتي أحدكم فيقول: من خلق السماوات والأرض؟
فيقول: الله.
فيقول: فمن خلقك؟
فيقول: الله.
فيقول: فمن خلق الله؟
فإذا حس أحدكم بذلك…»
فذكر بقية الحديث.
