٢٧٤ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما قال:
صلينا مع رسول الله ﷺ المغرب، فرجع من رجع، وعقَّب من عقَّب.
فجاء رسول الله ﷺ مسرعاً، قد حفزه النفس، وقد حسر عن ركبتيه، فقال:
«أبشروا! هذا ربكم قد فتح باباً من أبواب السماء، يباهي بكم الملائكة، يقول:
انظروا إلى عبادي، قد قضوا فريضة وهم ينتظرون أخرى».
صحيح: رواه ابن ماجه (٨٠١).

274 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr may Allah be pleased with them reported:
We prayed Maghrib with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Those who wished to leave departed, while others remained waiting.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then came quickly, breathing heavily from his haste, with his knees uncovered, and said:
“Rejoice! Your Lord has opened one of the gates of heaven and is expressing pride in you before the angels, saying:
‘Look at My servants. They have completed one obligatory prayer and are waiting for another.’”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (801).

٢٧٥ — عن أسامة بن زيد رضي الله عنهما قال:
قلت:
يا رسول الله، لم أرك تصوم شهراً من الشهور ما تصوم من شعبان؟
قال:
«ذلك شهر يغفل الناس عنه بين رجب ورمضان، وهو شهر تُرفع فيه الأعمال إلى رب العالمين، فأحب أن يُرفع عملي وأنا صائم».
حسن: رواه النسائي (٢٣٥٧).
ورواه الإمام أحمد (٢١٧٥٣)، وزاد في حديثه:
قلت:
يوم الاثنين ويوم الخميس؟
فقال:
«ذانك يومان تعرض فيهما الأعمال على رب العالمين، وأحب أن يعرض عملي وأنا صائم».

english_source:
275 — Usāmah ibn Zayd may Allah be pleased with them reported:
I asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, I have not seen you fast during any month as much as you fast during Shaʿbān.”
He replied:
“That is a month to which people are heedless, between Rajab and Ramaḍān. It is a month in which deeds are raised to the Lord of the worlds, and I love for my deeds to be raised while I am fasting.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (2357).
Imām Aḥmad (21753) also narrated it with the additional wording:
I asked:
“What about Monday and Thursday?”
He replied:
“Those are two days upon which deeds are presented to the Lord of the worlds, and I love for my deeds to be presented while I am fasting.”

٢٧٦ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«كان ملك الموت يأتي الناس عياناً، فأتى موسى عليه السلام فلطمه، فذهب بعينه، فرجع الملك إلى الله عز وجل وقال:
يا رب، بعثتني إلى موسى فلطمني فذهب بعيني…».
صحيح: ذكره الذهبي في العلو (٢٥) من صحيفة همام بن منبه، وهو فيها (٥٠).
وليس فيه:
«فعرج إلى ربه عز وجل»،
بل فيه:
«فرجع الملك إلى الله عز وجل».
وأصل هذا الحديث في الصحيحين وغيرهما مرفوعاً وموقوفاً.

276 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The Angel of Death used to come to people visibly. He came to Moses peace be upon him, and Moses struck him, causing his eye to be lost. So the angel returned to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and said:
‘My Lord, You sent me to Moses, and he struck me, causing my eye to be lost…’”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Al-Dhahabī mentioned it in al-ʿUluww (25) from the Ṣaḥīfah of Hammām ibn Munabbih, where it appears as no. 50.
That wording does not contain:
“He ascended to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic,”
but rather:
“The angel returned to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”
The core narration is found in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections and elsewhere in both marfūʿ and mawqūf forms.

٢٧٨ — عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«إذا مكث المني في الرحم أربعين ليلة، أتاه ملك النفوس فعرج به إلى الرب في راحته، فيقول:
أي رب، عبدك هذا ذكر أم أنثى؟
فيقضي الله إليه ما هو قاض.
ثم يقول:
أي رب، أشقي أم سعيد؟
فيكتب بين عينيه ما هو لاق».
قال:
وتلا أبو ذر من فاتحة التغابن خمس آيات.
حسن بالمتابعة: رواه عثمان بن سعيد الدارمي في الرد على الجهمية (٩٤).

٢٧٩ — عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال:
كنت جالساً مع رسول الله ﷺ في الحلقة، إذ جاء رجل فسلم على النبي ﷺ وعلى القوم، فقال:
السلام عليكم.
فرد عليه النبي ﷺ:
«وعليكم السلام ورحمة الله وبركاته».
فلما جلس الرجل قال:
الحمد لله كثيراً طيباً مباركاً فيه، كما يحب ربنا ويرضى.
فقال له النبي ﷺ:
«كيف قلت؟»
فرد على النبي ﷺ كما قال.
فقال النبي ﷺ:
«والذي نفسي بيده، لقد ابتدرها عشرة أملاك، كلهم حريص على أن يكتبوها، فما دروا كيف يكتبونها حتى رفعوه إلى ذي العزة، فقال:
اكتبوها كما قال عبدي».

english_source:
279 — Anas may Allah be pleased with him reported:
I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a gathering when a man came and greeted the Prophet ﷺ and the people, saying:
“Peace be upon you.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“And upon you be peace, the mercy of Allah, and His blessings.”
When the man sat down, he said:
“All praise belongs to Allah — abundant, good, and blessed praise — just as our Lord loves and is pleased with.”
The Prophet ﷺ asked him:
“How did you say it?”
He repeated exactly what he had said.
The Prophet ﷺ then said:
“By the One in whose Hand is my soul, ten angels rushed toward those words, each one eager to record them. They did not know how to record them until they raised them to the Possessor of Might.
He said:
‘Write them exactly as My servant said them.’”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (341) and Aḥmad (12612), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (845).

arabic_source:
٢٨٠ — عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«لما كانت الليلة التي أُسري بي فيها، أتت عليَّ رائحة طيبة، فقلت:
يا جبريل، ما هذه الرائحة الطيبة؟
فقال:
هذه رائحة ماشطة ابنة فرعون وأولادها.
قال:
قلت:
وما شأنها؟
قال:
بينا هي تمشط ابنة فرعون ذات يوم إذ سقطت المدرى من يدها، فقالت:
بسم الله.
فقالت لها ابنة فرعون:
أبي؟
قالت:
لا، ولكن ربي ورب أبيك الله.
قالت:
أخبره بذلك؟
قالت:
نعم.
فأخبرته، فدعاها، فقال:
يا فلانة، إن لك رباً غيري؟
قالت:
نعم، ربي وربك الله.
فأمر ببقرة من نحاس فأُحميت، ثم أمر بها أن تلقى هي وأولادها فيها.
قالت له:
إن لي إليك حاجة.
قال:
وما حاجتك؟
قالت:
أحب أن تجمع عظامي وعظام ولدي في ثوب واحد وتدفننا.
قال:
ذلك لك علينا من الحق.
قال:
فأمر بأولادها فأُلقوا بين يديها واحداً واحداً، إلى أن انتهى ذلك إلى صبي لها مرضع، كأنها تقاعست من أجله.
قال:
يا أمه، اقتحمي، فإن عذاب الدنيا أهون من عذاب الآخرة.
فاقتحمت».
وفي رواية قالت:
«ربي وربك الذي في السماء».
قال ابن عباس:
تكلم أربعة صغار: عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام، وصاحب جريج، وشاهد يوسف، وابن ماشطة ابنة فرعون.
وفي رواية قال:
«والرابع لا أحفظه».
صحيح: رواه الإمام أحمد (٢٨٢١)، وأبو يعلى (٢٥١٧)، والبزار في كشف الأستار (٥٤)، واللفظ لأحمد.

ما جاء عن الأئمة في صفة العلو
قال الذهبي في «العلو» (٣٣٢): «وبلغنا عن أبي مطيع الحكم بن عبد الله البلخي صاحب الفقه الأكبر قال: سألت أبا حنيفة عمن يقول: لا أعرف ربي في السماء أو في الأرض؟ فقال: قد كفر؛ لأن الله يقول: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى﴾ [طه: ٥] وعرشه فوق سماواته. فقلت له: إنه يقول: أقول على العرش استوى، ولكن قال: لا يدري العرش في السماء أو في الأرض؟ فقال: إذا أنكر أنه في السماء فقد كفر».
وقال أيضاً: «والله تعالى يُدعى من أعلى لا من أسفل؛ لأن الأسفل ليس وصف الربوبية والألوهية في شيء».
وقال مالك رحمه الله تعالى: «الله في السماء، وعلمه في كل مكان لا يخلو منه مكان». العلو (٣٤٣).
وقد سئل رحمه الله تعالى عن قوله: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى﴾ كيف استوى؟ فأطرق مالك وعلاه الرحضاء — يعني العرق — وانتظر القوم ما يجيء منه فيه، فرفع رأسه وقال: «الاستواء غير مجهول، والكيف غير معقول، والإيمان به واجب، والسؤال عنه بدعة، وأحسبك رجل سوء»، وأمر به فأُخرج. ذكره ابن قدامة في إثبات صفة العلو (ص ٢٨)، والبيهقي في الاعتقاد (ص ١١٦).
وذكر أبو عثمان الصابوني (ت ٤٤٩هـ) في كتاب الاعتقاد بلفظ: «الاستواء معلوم، والكيف مجهول، والإيمان به واجب، والسؤال عنه بدعة، وأظنك زنديقاً، فأخرجوه من المسجد».
وقال الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى: «القول في السنة التي أنا عليها، ورأيت أصحابنا عليها أهل الحديث الذين رأيتهم وأخذت عنهم: الإقرار بشهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، وأن محمداً رسول الله ﷺ، وأن الله تعالى على عرشه في سمائه، يقرب من خلقه كيف شاء، وأن الله تعالى ينزل إلى السماء الدنيا كيف شاء». ذكره الذهبي في «العلو» (٤٠٤) نحوه أو قريباً منه.
قال الحاكم: سمعت الأصم يقول: سمعت الربيع، سمعت الشافعي — وقد روى حديثاً — فقال له رجل: تأخذ بهذا يا أبا عبد الله؟ فقال: «إذا رويت حديثاً صحيحاً عن رسول الله ﷺ فلم آخذ به فأشهدكم أن عقلي قد ذهب». العلو (٤٠٦).
قال عبد الله بن أحمد: قيل لأبي: «ربنا تبارك وتعالى فوق السماء السابعة على عرشه، بائن من خلقه، وقدرته وعلمه بكل مكان؟» قال: «نعم، لا يخلو شيء من علمه». اجتماع الجيوش الإسلامية لابن القيم (١٣٥).
وبناء على هذه الأحاديث ذكر أئمة السلف بأنه يجوز السؤال عن الله تعالى بـ«أين»، ويجوز للمسؤول أن يقول إنه في السماء، ويشير إليه بالأصابع.
وأما القول بأن معنى المعية هو اختلاطه بالخلق بذاته، وأنه في كل مكان بذاته فهو قول باطل، قال به أهل الحلول وغلاة الصوفية، وأنهم أساؤوا إلى قدسيته، ولم يصونوه عن أقبح الأماكن وأقذرها. وقد تصدى للرد عليهم أئمة السلف الصالح كأبي حنيفة، ومالك، والشافعي، وأحمد، وإسحاق بن راهويه، وغيرهم، ومن أئمة الهدى كشيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية، وتلميذه ابن القيم وغيرهما، ومن الأئمة المجددين كشيخ الإسلام محمد بن عبد الوهاب رحمه الله تعالى، ومن المعاصرين كشيخ الإسلام ابن باز رحمه الله تعالى، وعلماء المملكة عموماً، وعلماء أهل السنة خصوصاً في أنحاء المعمورة.
وفسروا معنى قوله تعالى: ﴿وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾ [الحديد: ٤] ونحو ذلك من الآيات بأن المراد بالمعية علمه، وأنه تعالى فوق السماوات مستوٍ على العرش كما جاء في كتابه العزيز.
قال ابن عبد البر: «أجمع علماء الصحابة والتابعين الذين حمل عنهم التأويل قالوا في تأويل قوله تعالى: ﴿مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَجْوَى ثَلَاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ﴾ [المجادلة: ٧]: هو على العرش، وعلمه في كل مكان، وما خالفهم في ذلك أحد يحتج بقوله».
وقال سماحة الشيخ ابن باز رحمه الله تعالى: «وإن مما ثبت في القرآن والسنة، وأجمع عليه سلف الأمة أن الله تعالى فوق خلقه، بائن منهم، مستوٍ على عرشه استواء يليق بجلاله، لا يشابه خلقه في استوائهم، وهو سبحانه معهم بعلمه، لا تخفى عليه منهم خافية، وهذا هو ما يدل عليه القرآن بأبلغ العبارات وأوضحها، وما تدل عليه السنة بالأحاديث الصحيحة الصريحة». العقيدة الصحيحة وما يضادها (ص ٣٩).
وكلام السلف في هذا المعنى أكثر من أن يحصر.

هذه رائحة ماشطة ابنة فرعون وأولادها.

بسم الله.
فقالت لها ابنة فرعون:
أبي؟
قالت:
لا، ولكن ربي ورب أبيك الله.

أخبره بذلك؟

نعم.

يا فلانة، إن لك رباً غيري؟

نعم، ربي وربك الله.
فأمر ببقرة من نحاس فأُحميت، ثم أمر بها أن تلقى هي وأولادها فيها.

إن لي إليك حاجة.
قال:
وما حاجتك؟
قالت:
أحب أن تجمع عظامي وعظام ولدي في ثوب واحد وتدفننا.
قال:
ذلك لك علينا من الحق.
قال:
فأمر بأولادها فأُلقوا بين يديها واحداً واحداً، إلى أن انتهى ذلك إلى صبي لها مرضع، كأنها تقاعست من أجله.
قال:
يا أمه، اقتحمي، فإن عذاب الدنيا أهون من عذاب الآخرة.
فاقتحمت».
وفي رواية قالت:
«ربي وربك الذي في السماء».
قال ابن عباس:
تكلم أربعة صغار: عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام، وصاحب جريج، وشاهد يوسف، وابن ماشطة ابنة فرعون.
وفي رواية قال:
«والرابع لا أحفظه».
صحيح: رواه الإمام أحمد (٢٨٢١)، وأبو يعلى (٢٥١٧)، والبزار في كشف الأستار (٥٤)، واللفظ لأحمد.

ما جاء عن الأئمة في صفة العلو
قال الذهبي في «العلو» (٣٣٢): «وبلغنا عن أبي مطيع الحكم بن عبد الله البلخي صاحب الفقه الأكبر قال: سألت أبا حنيفة عمن يقول: لا أعرف ربي في السماء أو في الأرض؟ فقال: قد كفر؛ لأن الله يقول: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى﴾ [طه: ٥] وعرشه فوق سماواته. فقلت له: إنه يقول: أقول على العرش استوى، ولكن قال: لا يدري العرش في السماء أو في الأرض؟ فقال: إذا أنكر أنه في السماء فقد كفر».
وقال أيضاً: «والله تعالى يُدعى من أعلى لا من أسفل؛ لأن الأسفل ليس وصف الربوبية والألوهية في شيء».
وقال مالك رحمه الله تعالى: «الله في السماء، وعلمه في كل مكان لا يخلو منه مكان». العلو (٣٤٣).
وقد سئل رحمه الله تعالى عن قوله: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى﴾ كيف استوى؟ فأطرق مالك وعلاه الرحضاء — يعني العرق — وانتظر القوم ما يجيء منه فيه، فرفع رأسه وقال: «الاستواء غير مجهول، والكيف غير معقول، والإيمان به واجب، والسؤال عنه بدعة، وأحسبك رجل سوء»، وأمر به فأُخرج. ذكره ابن قدامة في إثبات صفة العلو (ص ٢٨)، والبيهقي في الاعتقاد (ص ١١٦).
وذكر أبو عثمان الصابوني (ت ٤٤٩هـ) في كتاب الاعتقاد بلفظ: «الاستواء معلوم، والكيف مجهول، والإيمان به واجب، والسؤال عنه بدعة، وأظنك زنديقاً، فأخرجوه من المسجد».
وقال الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى: «القول في السنة التي أنا عليها، ورأيت أصحابنا عليها أهل الحديث الذين رأيتهم وأخذت عنهم: الإقرار بشهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، وأن محمداً رسول الله ﷺ، وأن الله تعالى على عرشه في سمائه، يقرب من خلقه كيف شاء، وأن الله تعالى ينزل إلى السماء الدنيا كيف شاء». ذكره الذهبي في «العلو» (٤٠٤) نحوه أو قريباً منه.
قال الحاكم: سمعت الأصم يقول: سمعت الربيع، سمعت الشافعي — وقد روى حديثاً — فقال له رجل: تأخذ بهذا يا أبا عبد الله؟ فقال: «إذا رويت حديثاً صحيحاً عن رسول الله ﷺ فلم آخذ به فأشهدكم أن عقلي قد ذهب». العلو (٤٠٦).
قال عبد الله بن أحمد: قيل لأبي: «ربنا تبارك وتعالى فوق السماء السابعة على عرشه، بائن من خلقه، وقدرته وعلمه بكل مكان؟» قال: «نعم، لا يخلو شيء من علمه». اجتماع الجيوش الإسلامية لابن القيم (١٣٥).
وبناء على هذه الأحاديث ذكر أئمة السلف بأنه يجوز السؤال عن الله تعالى بـ«أين»، ويجوز للمسؤول أن يقول إنه في السماء، ويشير إليه بالأصابع.
وأما القول بأن معنى المعية هو اختلاطه بالخلق بذاته، وأنه في كل مكان بذاته فهو قول باطل، قال به أهل الحلول وغلاة الصوفية، وأنهم أساؤوا إلى قدسيته، ولم يصونوه عن أقبح الأماكن وأقذرها. وقد تصدى للرد عليهم أئمة السلف الصالح كأبي حنيفة، ومالك، والشافعي، وأحمد، وإسحاق بن راهويه، وغيرهم، ومن أئمة الهدى كشيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية، وتلميذه ابن القيم وغيرهما، ومن الأئمة المجددين كشيخ الإسلام محمد بن عبد الوهاب رحمه الله تعالى، ومن المعاصرين كشيخ الإسلام ابن باز رحمه الله تعالى، وعلماء المملكة عموماً، وعلماء أهل السنة خصوصاً في أنحاء المعمورة.
وفسروا معنى قوله تعالى: ﴿وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾ [الحديد: ٤] ونحو ذلك من الآيات بأن المراد بالمعية علمه، وأنه تعالى فوق السماوات مستوٍ على العرش كما جاء في كتابه العزيز.
قال ابن عبد البر: «أجمع علماء الصحابة والتابعين الذين حمل عنهم التأويل قالوا في تأويل قوله تعالى: ﴿مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَجْوَى ثَلَاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ﴾ [المجادلة: ٧]: هو على العرش، وعلمه في كل مكان، وما خالفهم في ذلك أحد يحتج بقوله».
وقال سماحة الشيخ ابن باز رحمه الله تعالى: «وإن مما ثبت في القرآن والسنة، وأجمع عليه سلف الأمة أن الله تعالى فوق خلقه، بائن منهم، مستوٍ على عرشه استواء يليق بجلاله، لا يشابه خلقه في استوائهم، وهو سبحانه معهم بعلمه، لا تخفى عليه منهم خافية، وهذا هو ما يدل عليه القرآن بأبلغ العبارات وأوضحها، وما تدل عليه السنة بالأحاديث الصحيحة الصريحة». العقيدة الصحيحة وما يضادها (ص ٣٩).
وكلام السلف في هذا المعنى أكثر من أن يحصر.

280 — Ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“On the night when I was taken on the Night Journey, a pleasant fragrance came to me.
I asked:
‘O Jibrīl, what is this pleasant fragrance?’
He replied:
‘This is the fragrance of the woman who combed the hair of Pharaoh’s daughter and of her children.’
I asked:
‘What was her story?’
He replied:
‘One day, while she was combing Pharaoh’s daughter’s hair, the comb fell from her hand, and she said:
“In the Name of Allah.”
Pharaoh’s daughter asked:
“My father?”
She replied:
“No. Rather, my Lord and your father’s Lord is Allah.”
She asked:
“Shall I tell him that?”
She replied:
“Yes.”
So she informed him.
Pharaoh summoned the woman and asked:
“O so-and-so, do you have a lord other than me?”
She replied:
“Yes. My Lord and your Lord is Allah.”
He ordered a large vessel of copper to be heated and then ordered that she and her children be thrown into it.
She said to him:
“I have one request of you.”
He asked:
“What is your request?”
She replied:
“I would like you to gather my bones and the bones of my children together in one cloth and bury us.”
He replied:
“That is a right you have upon us.”
He then ordered her children to be thrown before her one by one until it came to her nursing infant. She appeared to hesitate because of him.
The child said:
“O mother, plunge in, for the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter.”
So she plunged in.’”
In another narration, she said:
“My Lord and your Lord is the One who is in the heaven.”
Ibn ʿAbbās said:
“Four children spoke while still very young: Jesus son of Mary peace be upon him, the child associated with Jurayj, the witness of Joseph, and the son of the woman who combed Pharaoh’s daughter’s hair.”
In another narration he said:
“And the fourth, I do not remember.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Imām Aḥmad (2821), Abū Yaʿlā (2517), and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (54), with the wording of Aḥmad.

What the imams said regarding the Attribute of Highness/Exaltation (al-ʿuluww)
Al-Dhahabī said in al-ʿUluww (332): “It has reached us from Abū Muṭīʿ al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Balkhī, the author of al-Fiqh al-Akbar, that he said: ‘I asked Abū Ḥanīfah about someone who says: I do not know my Lord—whether He is in the heaven or on the earth. He said: He has disbelieved, because Allah says, “The Most Merciful rose over the Throne” [Ṭā Hā 20:5], and His Throne is above His heavens. I said: What if he says: I say He rose over the Throne, but I do not know whether the Throne is in the heaven or on the earth? He said: If he denies that it is in the heaven, then he has disbelieved.’”
He also said: “Allah Most High is called upon from above, not from below, because ‘below’ is not a description of Lordship or Divinity in any way.”
Mālik (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Allah is in the heaven, and His knowledge is in every place; nothing is devoid of His knowledge.” al-ʿUluww (343).
Mālik was asked about Allah’s statement, “The Most Merciful rose over the Throne” [Ṭā Hā 20:5]: “How did He rise over it?” Mālik lowered his head and sweat came over him while the people waited to see what he would say. He then raised his head and said: “The rising over is not unknown; the ‘how’ is not comprehensible; believing in it is obligatory; asking about it is an innovation; and I think you are a bad man.” He then ordered that the man be removed. Ibn Qudāmah mentioned it in Ithbāt Ṣifat al-ʿUluww (p. 28), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Iʿtiqād (p. 116).
Abū ʿUthmān al-Ṣābūnī (d. 449 AH) reported the wording: “The rising over is known, the ‘how’ is unknown, believing in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation; and I think you are a heretic, so remove him from the mosque.”
Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “The position regarding the Sunnah upon which I am, and upon which I saw our companions—the people of ḥadīth whom I met and learned from—is affirming the testimony that there is no deity except Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that Allah Most High is upon His Throne in His heaven; He draws near to His creation however He wills; and Allah Most High descends to the lowest heaven however He wills.” Al-Dhahabī mentioned it in al-ʿUluww (404), with this meaning or close to it.
Al-Ḥākim reported that al-Aṣamm said: I heard al-Rabīʿ say: I heard al-Shāfiʿī—after he narrated a ḥadīth—when a man said, “Do you take this, O Abū ʿAbdullāh?” He replied: “If I narrate an authentic ḥadīth from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and do not act upon it, then bear witness that my mind has gone.” al-ʿUluww (406).
ʿAbdullāh ibn Aḥmad said: It was said to my father: “Our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, is above the seventh heaven upon His Throne, distinct from His creation, while His power and knowledge are in every place?” He said: “Yes; nothing is devoid of His knowledge.” Ijtimāʿ al-Juyūsh al-Islāmiyyah by Ibn al-Qayyim (p. 135).
Based on these reports, the early imams stated that it is permissible to ask about Allah using “Where?”, and permissible for the one asked to say that He is in the heaven and to point upward with the fingers.
As for the claim that “being with” means that Allah mixes with creation in His Essence and that He is in every place in His Essence, this is a false statement attributed to people of incarnationism and extremists among some Ṣūfīs. The imams of the Salaf and later scholars refuted this view, including Abū Ḥanīfah, Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh, Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn al-Qayyim, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, Ibn Bāz, and other Sunni scholars.
They explained Allah’s statement, “And He is with you wherever you may be, and Allah sees all that you do” [al-Ḥadīd 57:4], and similar verses, as referring to His knowledge, while He is above the heavens and established over the Throne as stated in His Book.
Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: “The scholars among the Companions and the Tābiʿīn whose interpretations have been transmitted agreed regarding the interpretation of His statement, ‘There is no private conversation among three except that He is the fourth of them’ [al-Mujādilah 58:7], that He is over the Throne and His knowledge is in every place, and no one whose statement is relied upon differed with them.”
Shaykh Ibn Bāz (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Among what is established in the Qurʾān and Sunnah, and what the early generations of this Ummah agreed upon, is that Allah Most High is above His creation, distinct from them, established over His Throne in a manner befitting His majesty, not resembling created beings in their rising; and He is with them by His knowledge—nothing about them is hidden from Him. This is what the Qurʾān indicates in the clearest expressions and what the Sunnah indicates through authentic and explicit reports.” al-ʿAqīdah al-Ṣaḥīḥah wa-mā Yuḍāddihā (p. 39).
The statements of the Salaf on this meaning are too numerous to enumerate.

وقال أيضاً: «والله تعالى يُدعى من أعلى لا من أسفل؛ لأن الأسفل ليس وصف الربوبية والألوهية في شيء».
وقال مالك رحمه الله تعالى: «الله في السماء، وعلمه في كل مكان لا يخلو منه مكان». العلو (٣٤٣).
وقد سئل رحمه الله تعالى عن قوله: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى﴾ كيف استوى؟ فأطرق مالك وعلاه الرحضاء — يعني العرق — وانتظر القوم ما يجيء منه فيه، فرفع رأسه وقال: «الاستواء غير مجهول، والكيف غير معقول، والإيمان به واجب، والسؤال عنه بدعة، وأحسبك رجل سوء»، وأمر به فأُخرج. ذكره ابن قدامة في إثبات صفة العلو (ص ٢٨)، والبيهقي في الاعتقاد (ص ١١٦).
وذكر أبو عثمان الصابوني (ت ٤٤٩هـ) في كتاب الاعتقاد بلفظ: «الاستواء معلوم، والكيف مجهول، والإيمان به واجب، والسؤال عنه بدعة، وأظنك زنديقاً، فأخرجوه من المسجد».
وقال الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى: «القول في السنة التي أنا عليها، ورأيت أصحابنا عليها أهل الحديث الذين رأيتهم وأخذت عنهم: الإقرار بشهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، وأن محمداً رسول الله ﷺ، وأن الله تعالى على عرشه في سمائه، يقرب من خلقه كيف شاء، وأن الله تعالى ينزل إلى السماء الدنيا كيف شاء». ذكره الذهبي في «العلو» (٤٠٤) نحوه أو قريباً منه.
قال الحاكم: سمعت الأصم يقول: سمعت الربيع، سمعت الشافعي — وقد روى حديثاً — فقال له رجل: تأخذ بهذا يا أبا عبد الله؟ فقال: «إذا رويت حديثاً صحيحاً عن رسول الله ﷺ فلم آخذ به فأشهدكم أن عقلي قد ذهب». العلو (٤٠٦).
قال عبد الله بن أحمد: قيل لأبي: «ربنا تبارك وتعالى فوق السماء السابعة على عرشه، بائن من خلقه، وقدرته وعلمه بكل مكان؟» قال: «نعم، لا يخلو شيء من علمه». اجتماع الجيوش الإسلامية لابن القيم (١٣٥).
وبناء على هذه الأحاديث ذكر أئمة السلف بأنه يجوز السؤال عن الله تعالى بـ«أين»، ويجوز للمسؤول أن يقول إنه في السماء، ويشير إليه بالأصابع.
وأما القول بأن معنى المعية هو اختلاطه بالخلق بذاته، وأنه في كل مكان بذاته فهو قول باطل، قال به أهل الحلول وغلاة الصوفية، وأنهم أساؤوا إلى قدسيته، ولم يصونوه عن أقبح الأماكن وأقذرها. وقد تصدى للرد عليهم أئمة السلف الصالح كأبي حنيفة، ومالك، والشافعي، وأحمد، وإسحاق بن راهويه، وغيرهم، ومن أئمة الهدى كشيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية، وتلميذه ابن القيم وغيرهما، ومن الأئمة المجددين كشيخ الإسلام محمد بن عبد الوهاب رحمه الله تعالى، ومن المعاصرين كشيخ الإسلام ابن باز رحمه الله تعالى، وعلماء المملكة عموماً، وعلماء أهل السنة خصوصاً في أنحاء المعمورة.
وفسروا معنى قوله تعالى: ﴿وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾ [الحديد: ٤] ونحو ذلك من الآيات بأن المراد بالمعية علمه، وأنه تعالى فوق السماوات مستوٍ على العرش كما جاء في كتابه العزيز.
قال ابن عبد البر: «أجمع علماء الصحابة والتابعين الذين حمل عنهم التأويل قالوا في تأويل قوله تعالى: ﴿مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَجْوَى ثَلَاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ﴾ [المجادلة: ٧]: هو على العرش، وعلمه في كل مكان، وما خالفهم في ذلك أحد يحتج بقوله».
وقال سماحة الشيخ ابن باز رحمه الله تعالى: «وإن مما ثبت في القرآن والسنة، وأجمع عليه سلف الأمة أن الله تعالى فوق خلقه، بائن منهم، مستوٍ على عرشه استواء يليق بجلاله، لا يشابه خلقه في استوائهم، وهو سبحانه معهم بعلمه، لا تخفى عليه منهم خافية، وهذا هو ما يدل عليه القرآن بأبلغ العبارات وأوضحها، وما تدل عليه السنة بالأحاديث الصحيحة الصريحة». العقيدة الصحيحة وما يضادها (ص ٣٩).
وكلام السلف في هذا المعنى أكثر من أن يحصر.
280 — Ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“On the night when I was taken on the Night Journey, a pleasant fragrance came to me.
I asked:
‘O Jibrīl, what is this pleasant fragrance?’
He replied:
‘This is the fragrance of the woman who combed the hair of Pharaoh’s daughter and of her children.’
I asked:
‘What was her story?’
He replied:
‘One day, while she was combing Pharaoh’s daughter’s hair, the comb fell from her hand, and she said:
“In the Name of Allah.”
Pharaoh’s daughter asked:
“My father?”
She replied:
“No. Rather, my Lord and your father’s Lord is Allah.”
She asked:
“Shall I tell him that?”
She replied:
“Yes.”
So she informed him.
Pharaoh summoned the woman and asked:
“O so-and-so, do you have a lord other than me?”
She replied:
“Yes. My Lord and your Lord is Allah.”
He ordered a large vessel of copper to be heated and then ordered that she and her children be thrown into it.
She said to him:
“I have one request of you.”
He asked:
“What is your request?”
She replied:
“I would like you to gather my bones and the bones of my children together in one cloth and bury us.”
He replied:
“That is a right you have upon us.”
He then ordered her children to be thrown before her one by one until it came to her nursing infant. She appeared to hesitate because of him.
The child said:
“O mother, plunge in, for the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter.”
So she plunged in.’”
In another narration, she said:
“My Lord and your Lord is the One who is in the heaven.”
Ibn ʿAbbās said:
“Four children spoke while still very young: Jesus son of Mary peace be upon him, the child associated with Jurayj, the witness of Joseph, and the son of the woman who combed Pharaoh’s daughter’s hair.”
In another narration he said:
“And the fourth, I do not remember.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Imām Aḥmad (2821), Abū Yaʿlā (2517), and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (54), with the wording of Aḥmad.

What the imams said regarding the Attribute of Highness/Exaltation (al-ʿuluww)
Al-Dhahabī said in al-ʿUluww (332): “It has reached us from Abū Muṭīʿ al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Balkhī, the author of al-Fiqh al-Akbar, that he said: ‘I asked Abū Ḥanīfah about someone who says: I do not know my Lord—whether He is in the heaven or on the earth. He said: He has disbelieved, because Allah says, “The Most Merciful rose over the Throne” [Ṭā Hā 20:5], and His Throne is above His heavens. I said: What if he says: I say He rose over the Throne, but I do not know whether the Throne is in the heaven or on the earth? He said: If he denies that it is in the heaven, then he has disbelieved.’”
He also said: “Allah Most High is called upon from above, not from below, because ‘below’ is not a description of Lordship or Divinity in any way.”
Mālik (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Allah is in the heaven, and His knowledge is in every place; nothing is devoid of His knowledge.” al-ʿUluww (343).
Mālik was asked about Allah’s statement, “The Most Merciful rose over the Throne” [Ṭā Hā 20:5]: “How did He rise over it?” Mālik lowered his head and sweat came over him while the people waited to see what he would say. He then raised his head and said: “The rising over is not unknown; the ‘how’ is not comprehensible; believing in it is obligatory; asking about it is an innovation; and I think you are a bad man.” He then ordered that the man be removed. Ibn Qudāmah mentioned it in Ithbāt Ṣifat al-ʿUluww (p. 28), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Iʿtiqād (p. 116).
Abū ʿUthmān al-Ṣābūnī (d. 449 AH) reported the wording: “The rising over is known, the ‘how’ is unknown, believing in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation; and I think you are a heretic, so remove him from the mosque.”
Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “The position regarding the Sunnah upon which I am, and upon which I saw our companions—the people of ḥadīth whom I met and learned from—is affirming the testimony that there is no deity except Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that Allah Most High is upon His Throne in His heaven; He draws near to His creation however He wills; and Allah Most High descends to the lowest heaven however He wills.” Al-Dhahabī mentioned it in al-ʿUluww (404), with this meaning or close to it.
Al-Ḥākim reported that al-Aṣamm said: I heard al-Rabīʿ say: I heard al-Shāfiʿī—after he narrated a ḥadīth—when a man said, “Do you take this, O Abū ʿAbdullāh?” He replied: “If I narrate an authentic ḥadīth from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and do not act upon it, then bear witness that my mind has gone.” al-ʿUluww (406).
ʿAbdullāh ibn Aḥmad said: It was said to my father: “Our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, is above the seventh heaven upon His Throne, distinct from His creation, while His power and knowledge are in every place?” He said: “Yes; nothing is devoid of His knowledge.” Ijtimāʿ al-Juyūsh al-Islāmiyyah by Ibn al-Qayyim (p. 135).
Based on these reports, the early imams stated that it is permissible to ask about Allah using “Where?”, and permissible for the one asked to say that He is in the heaven and to point upward with the fingers.
As for the claim that “being with” means that Allah mixes with creation in His Essence and that He is in every place in His Essence, this is a false statement attributed to people of incarnationism and extremists among some Ṣūfīs. The imams of the Salaf and later scholars refuted this view, including Abū Ḥanīfah, Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh, Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn al-Qayyim, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, Ibn Bāz, and other Sunni scholars.
They explained Allah’s statement, “And He is with you wherever you may be, and Allah sees all that you do” [al-Ḥadīd 57:4], and similar verses, as referring to His knowledge, while He is above the heavens and established over the Throne as stated in His Book.
Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: “The scholars among the Companions and the Tābiʿīn whose interpretations have been transmitted agreed regarding the interpretation of His statement, ‘There is no private conversation among three except that He is the fourth of them’ [al-Mujādilah 58:7], that He is over the Throne and His knowledge is in every place, and no one whose statement is relied upon differed with them.”
Shaykh Ibn Bāz (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Among what is established in the Qurʾān and Sunnah, and what the early generations of this Ummah agreed upon, is that Allah Most High is above His creation, distinct from them, established over His Throne in a manner befitting His majesty, not resembling created beings in their rising; and He is with them by His knowledge—nothing about them is hidden from Him. This is what the Qurʾān indicates in the clearest expressions and what the Sunnah indicates through authentic and explicit reports.” al-ʿAqīdah al-Ṣaḥīḥah wa-mā Yuḍāddihā (p. 39).
The statements of the Salaf on this meaning are too numerous to enumerate.

قال ابن عبد البر: «أجمع علماء الصحابة والتابعين الذين حمل عنهم التأويل قالوا في تأويل قوله تعالى: ﴿مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَجْوَى ثَلَاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ﴾ [المجادلة: ٧]: هو على العرش، وعلمه في كل مكان، وما خالفهم في ذلك أحد يحتج بقوله».
وقال سماحة الشيخ ابن باز رحمه الله تعالى: «وإن مما ثبت في القرآن والسنة، وأجمع عليه سلف الأمة أن الله تعالى فوق خلقه، بائن منهم، مستوٍ على عرشه استواء يليق بجلاله، لا يشابه خلقه في استوائهم، وهو سبحانه معهم بعلمه، لا تخفى عليه منهم خافية، وهذا هو ما يدل عليه القرآن بأبلغ العبارات وأوضحها، وما تدل عليه السنة بالأحاديث الصحيحة الصريحة». العقيدة الصحيحة وما يضادها (ص ٣٩).
وكلام السلف في هذا المعنى أكثر من أن يحصر.
280 — Ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“On the night when I was taken on the Night Journey, a pleasant fragrance came to me.
I asked:
‘O Jibrīl, what is this pleasant fragrance?’
He replied:
‘This is the fragrance of the woman who combed the hair of Pharaoh’s daughter and of her children.’
I asked:
‘What was her story?’
He replied:
‘One day, while she was combing Pharaoh’s daughter’s hair, the comb fell from her hand, and she said:
“In the Name of Allah.”
Pharaoh’s daughter asked:
“My father?”
She replied:
“No. Rather, my Lord and your father’s Lord is Allah.”
She asked:
“Shall I tell him that?”
She replied:
“Yes.”
So she informed him.
Pharaoh summoned the woman and asked:
“O so-and-so, do you have a lord other than me?”
She replied:
“Yes. My Lord and your Lord is Allah.”
He ordered a large vessel of copper to be heated and then ordered that she and her children be thrown into it.
She said to him:
“I have one request of you.”
He asked:
“What is your request?”
She replied:
“I would like you to gather my bones and the bones of my children together in one cloth and bury us.”
He replied:
“That is a right you have upon us.”
He then ordered her children to be thrown before her one by one until it came to her nursing infant. She appeared to hesitate because of him.
The child said:
“O mother, plunge in, for the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter.”
So she plunged in.’”
In another narration, she said:
“My Lord and your Lord is the One who is in the heaven.”
Ibn ʿAbbās said:
“Four children spoke while still very young: Jesus son of Mary peace be upon him, the child associated with Jurayj, the witness of Joseph, and the son of the woman who combed Pharaoh’s daughter’s hair.”
In another narration he said:
“And the fourth, I do not remember.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Imām Aḥmad (2821), Abū Yaʿlā (2517), and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (54), with the wording of Aḥmad.

What the imams said regarding the Attribute of Highness/Exaltation (al-ʿuluww)
Al-Dhahabī said in al-ʿUluww (332): “It has reached us from Abū Muṭīʿ al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Balkhī, the author of al-Fiqh al-Akbar, that he said: ‘I asked Abū Ḥanīfah about someone who says: I do not know my Lord—whether He is in the heaven or on the earth. He said: He has disbelieved, because Allah says, “The Most Merciful rose over the Throne” [Ṭā Hā 20:5], and His Throne is above His heavens. I said: What if he says: I say He rose over the Throne, but I do not know whether the Throne is in the heaven or on the earth? He said: If he denies that it is in the heaven, then he has disbelieved.’”
He also said: “Allah Most High is called upon from above, not from below, because ‘below’ is not a description of Lordship or Divinity in any way.”
Mālik (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Allah is in the heaven, and His knowledge is in every place; nothing is devoid of His knowledge.” al-ʿUluww (343).
Mālik was asked about Allah’s statement, “The Most Merciful rose over the Throne” [Ṭā Hā 20:5]: “How did He rise over it?” Mālik lowered his head and sweat came over him while the people waited to see what he would say. He then raised his head and said: “The rising over is not unknown; the ‘how’ is not comprehensible; believing in it is obligatory; asking about it is an innovation; and I think you are a bad man.” He then ordered that the man be removed. Ibn Qudāmah mentioned it in Ithbāt Ṣifat al-ʿUluww (p. 28), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Iʿtiqād (p. 116).
Abū ʿUthmān al-Ṣābūnī (d. 449 AH) reported the wording: “The rising over is known, the ‘how’ is unknown, believing in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation; and I think you are a heretic, so remove him from the mosque.”
Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “The position regarding the Sunnah upon which I am, and upon which I saw our companions—the people of ḥadīth whom I met and learned from—is affirming the testimony that there is no deity except Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that Allah Most High is upon His Throne in His heaven; He draws near to His creation however He wills; and Allah Most High descends to the lowest heaven however He wills.” Al-Dhahabī mentioned it in al-ʿUluww (404), with this meaning or close to it.
Al-Ḥākim reported that al-Aṣamm said: I heard al-Rabīʿ say: I heard al-Shāfiʿī—after he narrated a ḥadīth—when a man said, “Do you take this, O Abū ʿAbdullāh?” He replied: “If I narrate an authentic ḥadīth from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and do not act upon it, then bear witness that my mind has gone.” al-ʿUluww (406).
ʿAbdullāh ibn Aḥmad said: It was said to my father: “Our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, is above the seventh heaven upon His Throne, distinct from His creation, while His power and knowledge are in every place?” He said: “Yes; nothing is devoid of His knowledge.” Ijtimāʿ al-Juyūsh al-Islāmiyyah by Ibn al-Qayyim (p. 135).
Based on these reports, the early imams stated that it is permissible to ask about Allah using “Where?”, and permissible for the one asked to say that He is in the heaven and to point upward with the fingers.
As for the claim that “being with” means that Allah mixes with creation in His Essence and that He is in every place in His Essence, this is a false statement attributed to people of incarnationism and extremists among some Ṣūfīs. The imams of the Salaf and later scholars refuted this view, including Abū Ḥanīfah, Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh, Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn al-Qayyim, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, Ibn Bāz, and other Sunni scholars.
They explained Allah’s statement, “And He is with you wherever you may be, and Allah sees all that you do” [al-Ḥadīd 57:4], and similar verses, as referring to His knowledge, while He is above the heavens and established over the Throne as stated in His Book.
Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: “The scholars among the Companions and the Tābiʿīn whose interpretations have been transmitted agreed regarding the interpretation of His statement, ‘There is no private conversation among three except that He is the fourth of them’ [al-Mujādilah 58:7], that He is over the Throne and His knowledge is in every place, and no one whose statement is relied upon differed with them.”
Shaykh Ibn Bāz (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Among what is established in the Qurʾān and Sunnah, and what the early generations of this Ummah agreed upon, is that Allah Most High is above His creation, distinct from them, established over His Throne in a manner befitting His majesty, not resembling created beings in their rising; and He is with them by His knowledge—nothing about them is hidden from Him. This is what the Qurʾān indicates in the clearest expressions and what the Sunnah indicates through authentic and explicit reports.” al-ʿAqīdah al-Ṣaḥīḥah wa-mā Yuḍāddihā (p. 39).
The statements of the Salaf on this meaning are too numerous to enumerate.

٢٨١ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«لما قضى الله الخلق كتب في كتابه، فهو عنده فوق العرش: إن رحمتي غلبت غضبي».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣١٩٤)، ومسلم (٢٧٥١).
قال ابن خزيمة:
«هذا الخبر دال على أن ربنا جل وعلا فوق عرشه، الذي كتابه: إن رحمته غلبت غضبه، عنده».

281 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When Allah completed the creation, He wrote in His Book — which is with Him above the Throne:
‘Indeed, My mercy has overcome My wrath.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3194) and Muslim (2751).
Ibn Khuzaymah said:
“This report indicates that our Lord, Majestic and Exalted, is above His Throne, and that His Book containing the words, ‘Indeed, My mercy has overcome My wrath,’ is with Him.”

٢٨٢ — عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه قال:
قال النبي ﷺ لأبي ذر حين غربت الشمس:
«أتدري أين تذهب؟»
قلت:
الله ورسوله أعلم.
قال:
«فإنها تذهب حتى تسجد تحت العرش…».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣١٩٩)، ومسلم (١٥٩).
وفي رواية قال أبو ذر:
سألت رسول الله ﷺ عن قول الله تعالى:
﴿وَالشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَهَا﴾
 [يس: ٣٨]
قال:
«مستقرها تحت العرش».

english_source:
282 — Abū Dharr may Allah be pleased with him reported:
When the sun set, the Prophet ﷺ asked Abū Dharr:
“Do you know where it goes?”
I replied:
“Allah and His Messenger know best.”
He said:
“It goes until it prostrates beneath the Throne…”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3199) and Muslim (159).
In another narration, Abū Dharr said:
I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning the statement of Allah Most High:
“And the sun runs to its resting place.”
 [Sūrat Yā Sīn 36:38]
He replied:
“Its resting place is beneath the Throne.”

“The bond of kinship is suspended from the Throne, saying:
‘Whoever maintains me, Allah will maintain him; and whoever cuts me off, Allah will cut him off.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Muslim (2555) and al-Bukhārī (5989).

«إن الرحم معلقة بالعرش، وليس الواصل بالمكافئ، ولكن الواصل الذي إذا انقطعت رحمه وصلها».

285 — Wahb ibn Jābir al-Khaywānī reported:
I was with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ may Allah be pleased with them when a steward of his arrived from al-Shām, with only one night of Ramaḍān remaining.
ʿAbdullāh asked him:
“Did you leave with my family enough to provide for them?”
He replied:
“I left them some money for their expenses.”
ʿAbdullāh said:
“I insist that when you return, you leave them enough to provide for them, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘It is sufficient sin for a man that he neglect those whom he is responsible for supporting.’”
Then he began narrating to us and said:
“Indeed, when the sun sets, it gives salām, prostrates, and seeks permission, and permission is granted to it.
Then a day will come when it sets, gives salām, prostrates, and seeks permission, but permission will not be granted to it.
It will say:
‘My Lord, the journey is long, and if permission is not granted to me, I will not reach my destination.’
It will then be held for as long as Allah wills.
Then it will be said to it:
‘Rise from the place where you set.’
From that day until the Day of Resurrection:
‘No soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before.’”
 [Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:158]
He then mentioned Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj and said:
“A man among them will not die until one thousand descendants have been born from his loins. Beyond them are three nations whose numbers no one knows except Allah: Mansak, Tāwīl, and Tāwīs.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzāq in al-Muṣannaf (20810) and al-Ḥākim (4/500–501).

٢٨٦ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«أنا سيد الناس يوم القيامة…».
فذكر حديث الشفاعة الطويل، وهو مخرج في موضعه، وفيه:
«فأنطلق فآتي تحت العرش، فأقع ساجداً لربي، ثم يفتح الله علي ويلهمني من محامده وحسن الثناء عليه شيئاً لم يفتحه لأحد قبلي…».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٧١٢)، ومسلم (١٩٤).

286 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“I will be the master of mankind on the Day of Resurrection…”
He then narrated the lengthy ḥadīth of intercession, which is presented in full in its proper place. Among its words are:
“Then I will go and come beneath the Throne, and I will fall down in prostration before my Lord. Allah will then open for me and inspire me with forms of praise and beautiful glorification of Him that He had not opened for anyone before me…”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4712) and Muslim (194).

٢٨٧ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«سبعة يظلهم الله في ظله، يوم لا ظل إلا ظله…».
وساق الحديث، وهو مذكور في موضعه.
متفق عليه: رواه مالك (١٤)، ومسلم (١٠٣١)، والبخاري (٦٦٠).
وقوله:
«في ظله»
أي: ظل عرشه.

287 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Seven will be shaded by Allah in His shade on the Day when there will be no shade except His shade…”
He then narrated the remainder of the ḥadīth, which is recorded in its proper place.
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik (14), Muslim (1031), and al-Bukhārī (660).
The words:
“In His shade”
mean: the shade of His Throne.

٢٨٨ — عن مسروق قال:
سألنا عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن هذه الآية:
﴿وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ أَمْوَاتًا بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ﴾
 [آل عمران: ١٦٩]
فقال:
أما إنا قد سألنا عن ذلك، فقال:
«أرواحهم في جوف طير خضر، لها قناديل معلقة بالعرش، تسرح من الجنة حيث شاءت، ثم تأوي إلى تلك القناديل».
فذكر الحديث بطوله.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٨٧).
وقوله:
«سألنا عن ذلك»
الظاهر أن المسؤول هو النبي ﷺ، وحذفه لظهور العلم به، كما قال ابن القيم في تهذيب السنن (٣/٣٧٤).

288 — Masrūq reported:
We asked ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd may Allah be pleased with him concerning the verse:
“Do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.”
 [Āl ʿImrān 3:169]
He replied:
“We indeed asked about that, and he said:
‘Their souls are within green birds. They have lamps suspended from the Throne. They roam freely in Paradise wherever they wish, then return to those lamps.’”
He then mentioned the remainder of the lengthy ḥadīth.
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (1887).
Regarding the words:
“We asked about that,”
the apparent meaning is that the one who was asked was the Prophet ﷺ. He was not explicitly named because this was already understood, as Ibn al-Qayyim stated in Tahdhīb al-Sunan (3/374).

٢٨٩ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«يجمع الله الأولين والآخرين لميقات يوم معلوم أربعين سنة، شاخصة أبصارهم إلى السماء ينتظرون فصل القضاء، وينزل الله في ظلل من الغمام من العرش إلى الكرسي…».
الحديث بطوله.
حسن: رواه ابن منده في التوحيد (٥٣١).

289 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Allah will gather the first and the last generations for the appointed time of a known Day for forty years, their eyes fixed toward the heaven as they await the decisive judgment. Allah will descend in canopies of clouds from the Throne to the Kursī…”
The ḥadīth continues at length.
Ḥasan: Narrated by Ibn Mandah in al-Tawḥīd (531).

“Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will say on the Day of Resurrection:
‘Where are those who loved one another for My majesty? Today I will shade them in My shade, on the Day when there will be no shade except My shade.’”

I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said:
‘My love has become obligatory for those who love one another for My sake, those who sit together for My sake, those who visit one another for My sake, and those who give generously to one another for My sake.’”

292 — Muʿādh ibn Jabal may Allah be pleased with him reported:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said:
‘My love has become obligatory for those who love one another for My sake, those who sit together for My sake, those who visit one another for My sake, and those who give generously to one another for My sake.’”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Mālik (16).

٢٩٣ — عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:

٢٩٤ — عن أبي مالك الأشعري رضي الله عنه قال:
كنت عند رسول الله ﷺ، فنزلت هذه الآية:
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَسْأَلُوا عَنْ أَشْيَاءَ إِنْ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ﴾
 [المائدة: ١٠١]
قالوا:
فنحن نسأله إذاً.
قال:
«إن لله عباداً ليسوا بأنبياء ولا شهداء، يغبطهم النبيون والشهداء بقربهم ومقعدهم من الله يوم القيامة».
قال:
وفي ناحية القوم أعرابي، فقام فحثا على وجهه، ورمى بيديه، ثم قال:
حدثنا يا رسول الله عنهم، من هم؟
قال:
فرأيت وجه رسول الله ﷺ أبشر.
فقال النبي ﷺ:
«هم عباد من عباد الله من بلدان شتى، وقبائل شتى، من شعوب القبائل، لم يكن بينهم أرحام يتواصلون بها، ولا دنيا يتباذلون بها، تحابوا بروح الله، يجعل الله وجوههم نوراً، ويجعل لهم منابر من لؤلؤ قدام الرحمن، يفزع الناس ولا يفزعون، ويخاف الناس ولا يخافون».
حسن: رواه عبد الرزاق (٢٠٣٢٤)، وعبد الله بن المبارك في الزهد (٧١٤)، وأحمد (٢٢٩٠٦).

294 — Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī may Allah be pleased with him reported:
I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when the following verse was revealed:
“O you who believe, do not ask about matters which, if disclosed to you, would distress you.”
 [Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:101]
They said:
“Then we will ask him.”
He said:
“Indeed, Allah has servants who are neither prophets nor martyrs, yet the prophets and martyrs will envy them on the Day of Resurrection because of their nearness and their station with Allah.”
At the edge of the gathering was a Bedouin. He rose, fell forward eagerly, extended his hands, and said:
“Tell us about them, O Messenger of Allah. Who are they?”
I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ brighten.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“They are servants from among the servants of Allah, from different lands and different tribes, from scattered peoples. They share no ties of kinship through which they maintain relations, nor worldly wealth that they exchange with one another. Rather, they love one another through the Spirit of Allah.
Allah will make their faces light and will place for them pulpits of pearl before al-Raḥmān. The people will be terrified while they will not be terrified, and the people will fear while they will not fear.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzāq (20324), ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak in al-Zuhd (714), and Aḥmad (22906).

٢٩٥ — عن أبي إدريس عائذ الله قال:
مر رجل فقمت إليه، فقلت:
إن هذا حدثني بحديث رسول الله ﷺ، فهل سمعته؟ يعني معاذاً.
قال:
ما كان يحدثك إلا حقاً.
فأخبرته.
قال:
قد سمعت هذا من رسول الله ﷺ — يعني المتحابين في الله يظلهم الله في ظل عرشه يوم لا ظل إلا ظله — وما هو أفضل منه.
قلت:
أي رحمك الله، وما هو أفضل منه؟
قال:
سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يأثر عن الله عز وجل، قال:
«حقت محبتي للمتحابين فيَّ، وحقت محبتي للمتواصلين فيَّ، وحقت محبتي للمتزاورين فيَّ، وحقت محبتي للمتباذلين فيَّ».
ولا أدري بأيها بدأ.
قلت:
من أنت، رحمك الله؟
قال:
أنا عبادة بن الصامت.
صحيح: رواه الحاكم (٤/١٦٩)، وأحمد (٢٢٠٠٢).

295 — Abū Idrīs ʿĀʾidhullāh reported:
A man passed by, so I stood up to him and said:
“This man narrated to me a ḥadīth from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Have you heard it?” — meaning Muʿādh.
He replied:
“He would only narrate to you what is true.”
So I told him the narration.
He said:
“I heard this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ” — meaning that those who love one another for Allah’s sake will be shaded by Allah beneath the shade of His Throne on the Day when there is no shade except His shade — “and there is something even better than that.”
I asked:
“May Allah have mercy upon you! What is better than that?”
He replied:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrate from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He said:
“My love has become due for those who love one another for My sake. My love has become due for those who maintain relations with one another for My sake. My love has become due for those who visit one another for My sake. And My love has become due for those who give generously to one another for My sake.”
I do not know with which of these he began.
I asked:
“Who are you, may Allah have mercy upon you?”
He replied:
“I am ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit.”

٢٩٥ — عن أبي إدريس عائذ الله قال:
مر رجل فقمت إليه، فقلت:
إن هذا حدثني بحديث رسول الله ﷺ، فهل سمعته؟ يعني معاذاً.
قال:
ما كان يحدثك إلا حقاً.
فأخبرته.
قال:
قد سمعت هذا من رسول الله ﷺ — يعني المتحابين في الله يظلهم الله في ظل عرشه يوم لا ظل إلا ظله — وما هو أفضل منه.
قلت:
أي رحمك الله، وما هو أفضل منه؟
قال:
سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يأثر عن الله عز وجل، قال:
«حقت محبتي للمتحابين فيَّ، وحقت محبتي للمتواصلين فيَّ، وحقت محبتي للمتزاورين فيَّ، وحقت محبتي للمتباذلين فيَّ».
ولا أدري بأيها بدأ.
قلت:
من أنت، رحمك الله؟
قال:
أنا عبادة بن الصامت.
صحيح: رواه الحاكم (٤/١٦٩)، وأحمد (٢٢٠٠٢).

“Indeed, ever since the bearer of the Trumpet was entrusted with it, his gaze has remained fixed and ready, looking toward the Throne out of fear that he may be commanded before his glance can return to him. His eyes are like two brilliant stars.”

٢٩٧ — عن جابر رضي الله عنه قال:
لما رجعت إلى رسول الله ﷺ مهاجرة البحر، قال:
«ألا تحدثوني بأعاجيب ما رأيتم بأرض الحبشة؟»
قال فتية منهم:
بلى يا رسول الله.
بينا نحن جلوس مرت بنا عجوز من عجائز رهابينهم تحمل على رأسها قلة من ماء، فمرت بفتى منهم، فجعل إحدى يديه بين كتفيها، ثم دفعها، فخرت على ركبتيها، فانكسرت قلتها.
فلما ارتفعت التفتت إليه، فقالت:
سوف تعلم يا غدر! إذا وضع الله الكرسي، وجمع الأولين والآخرين، وتكلمت الأيدي والأرجل بما كانوا يكسبون، فسوف تعلم كيف أمري وأمرك عنده غداً.
قال:
فقال رسول الله ﷺ:
«صدقت، صدقت. كيف يقدس الله أمة لا يؤخذ لضعيفهم من شديدهم؟»
حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٤٠١٠)، وابن حبان (٥٠٥٨)، وابن أبي الدنيا في الأهوال (٢٤٢).

297 — Jābir may Allah be pleased with him reported:
When the emigrants who had crossed the sea returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he asked:
“Will you not tell me about some of the remarkable things you saw in the land of Abyssinia?”
Some young men among them replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah.
While we were sitting, an elderly woman from among their devoted worshippers passed by us carrying a water vessel upon her head.
A young man passed by her, placed one of his hands between her shoulders, and pushed her. She fell upon her knees, and her water vessel broke.
When she rose, she turned toward him and said:
‘You will soon know, O treacherous one! When Allah sets up the Kursī, gathers the first and the last, and the hands and feet speak concerning what they used to earn, then you will know tomorrow how my affair and your affair will be before Him.’”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“She spoke the truth. She spoke the truth. How can Allah sanctify a nation in which the right of its weak is not taken from its strong?”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (4010), Ibn Ḥibbān (5058), and Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in al-Ahwāl (242).

٢٩٨ — عن بريدة رضي الله عنه قال:
سأل رسول الله ﷺ جعفراً حين قدم من الحبشة:
«ما أعجب شيء رأيته؟»
قال:
رأيت امرأة تحمل على رأسها مكتلاً من طعام، فمر فارس فركضه فأبذره، فجلست تجمع طعامها، ثم التفتت فقالت:
ويل لك! إذا وضع الملك تبارك وتعالى كرسيه، فأخذ للمظلوم من الظالم.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ تصديقاً لقولها:
«لا قدست أمة — أو: كيف تقدس أمة — لا يأخذ ضعيفها حقه من شديدها، وهو غير متعتع».
حسن بالشواهد: رواه البزار في كشف الأستار (١٥٩٦)، والبيهقي في الأسماء والصفات (٨٦٠).

298 — Buraydah may Allah be pleased with him reported:
When Jaʿfar returned from Abyssinia, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him:
“What was the most remarkable thing you saw?”
He replied:
“I saw a woman carrying a basket of food upon her head. A horseman passed by and struck it, scattering its contents.
She sat down gathering her food, then turned toward him and said:
‘Woe to you! When the King, Blessed and Exalted, sets up His Kursī and takes the right of the oppressed from the oppressor…’”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said in confirmation of her words:
“A nation is not sanctified — or: How can a nation be sanctified? — if its weak cannot obtain his right from its strong without intimidation or difficulty.”
Ḥasan due to supporting narrations: Narrated by al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (1596) and al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa al-Ṣifāt (860).

«ما أعجب شيء رأيته؟»
قال:
رأيت امرأة تحمل على رأسها مكتلاً من طعام، فمر فارس فركضه فأبذره، فجلست تجمع طعامها، ثم التفتت فقالت:
ويل لك! إذا وضع الملك تبارك وتعالى كرسيه، فأخذ للمظلوم من الظالم.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ تصديقاً لقولها:
«لا قدست أمة — أو: كيف تقدس أمة — لا يأخذ ضعيفها حقه من شديدها، وهو غير متعتع».
حسن بالشواهد: رواه البزار في كشف الأستار (١٥٩٦)، والبيهقي في الأسماء والصفات (٨٦٠).
298 — Buraydah may Allah be pleased with him reported:
When Jaʿfar returned from Abyssinia, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him:
“What was the most remarkable thing you saw?”
He replied:
“I saw a woman carrying a basket of food upon her head. A horseman passed by and struck it, scattering its contents.
She sat down gathering her food, then turned toward him and said:
‘Woe to you! When the King, Blessed and Exalted, sets up His Kursī and takes the right of the oppressed from the oppressor…’”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said in confirmation of her words:
“A nation is not sanctified — or: How can a nation be sanctified? — if its weak cannot obtain his right from its strong without intimidation or difficulty.”
Ḥasan due to supporting narrations: Narrated by al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (1596) and al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa al-Ṣifāt (860).

«ينزل الله تبارك وتعالى كل ليلة إلى السماء الدنيا حين يبقى ثلث الليل الآخر، فيقول: من يدعوني فأستجيب له؟ من يسألني فأعطيه؟ من يستغفرني فأغفر له؟»

«حتى يضيء الفجر».

299 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Allah, Blessed and Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven when the final third of the night remains and says:
‘Who is calling upon Me so that I may answer him? Who is asking Me so that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness so that I may forgive him?’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik in al-Qurʾān (30) and al-Bukhārī (1145).
Muslim (758) also narrated it with the additional wording:
“Until the dawn begins to shine.”

٣٠٠ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهما قالا: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«إن الله يمهل حتى إذا ذهب ثلث الليل الأول نزل إلى السماء الدنيا، فيقول: هل من مستغفر؟ هل من تائب؟ هل من سائل؟ هل من داع؟ حتى ينفجر الفجر».
صحيح: رواه مسلم في صلاة المسافرين (٧٥٨: ١٧٢).

300 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with them reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Allah gives respite until the first third of the night has passed. Then He descends to the lowest heaven and says:
‘Is there anyone seeking forgiveness? Is there anyone repenting? Is there anyone asking? Is there anyone supplicating?’
This continues until dawn breaks.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim in Ṣalāt al-Musāfirīn (758:172).

٣٠١ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«ينزل الله في السماء الدنيا لشطر الليل، أو لثلث الليل الآخر، فيقول: من يدعوني فأستجيب له، أو يسألني فأعطيه؟ ثم يقول: من يُقرض غير عديم ولا ظلوم؟»

«غير عديم»
قال أهل اللغة: يقال أعدم الرجل إذا افتقر، فهو معدم وعديم وعدوم.

301 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Allah descends to the lowest heaven at the middle of the night, or during the last third of the night, and says:
‘Who is calling upon Me so that I may answer him, or asking Me so that I may give him?’
Then He says:
‘Who will lend to One who is neither poor nor unjust?’”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim in Ṣalāt al-Musāfirīn (758:171).
Regarding the expression:
“Neither poor,”
the scholars of the Arabic language said that a man is described as aʿdama when he becomes poor; hence the forms muʿdim, ʿadīm, and ʿadūm.

حدثني رسول الله ﷺ:
«إن الله عز وجل إذا كان يوم القيامة نزل إلى العباد ليقضي بينهم».

وأصل هذا الحديث في صحيح مسلم من وجه آخر، إلا أنه ليس فيه ذكر النزول (١٩٠٥).

302 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ told me:
“Indeed, when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will descend to the servants to judge between them.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2382), and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (2482) and al-Ḥākim (1/418–419).
The basis of this ḥadīth is also found in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim through another route, but without mention of the descent (1905).

٣٠٣ — عن رفاعة الجهني رضي الله عنه قال:
أقبلنا مع رسول الله ﷺ حتى إذا كنا بالكديد — أو قال: بقُديد — جعل رجال منا يستأذنون إلى أهليهم، فيأذن لهم.
فقام رسول الله ﷺ، فحمد الله وأثنى عليه، ثم قال:
«ما بال رجال يكون شق الشجرة التي تلي رسول الله ﷺ أبغض إليهم من الشق الآخر؟»
فلم نر عند ذلك من القوم إلا باكياً.
فقال رجل:
إن الذي يستأذنك بعد هذا لسفيه.
فحمد الله وقال حينئذ:
«أشهد عند الله: لا يموت عبد يشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأني رسول الله، صدقاً من قلبه، ثم يسدد، إلا سلك في الجنة».
قال:

303 — Rifāʿah al-Juhanī may Allah be pleased with him reported:
We were traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we reached al-Kudayd — or he said Qudayd. Some men among us began asking permission to go to their families, and he gave them permission.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then stood, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said:
“What is the matter with some men that the side of the tree nearest to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more disliked by them than its other side?”
At that, we saw no one among the people except that he was weeping.
A man said:
“Whoever asks your permission after this is surely foolish.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ praised Allah and then said:
“I testify before Allah that no servant dies while testifying that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah, truthfully from his heart, and then strives to remain upright, except that he will enter Paradise.”
He continued:
“My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has promised me that He will admit seventy thousand from my Ummah without reckoning and without punishment. I hope that they will not enter it until you, together with the righteous among your fathers, spouses, and descendants, have taken up your dwellings in Paradise.”
He also said:
“When half the night has passed — or he said two-thirds of the night — Allah, Mighty and Majestic, descends to the lowest heaven and says:
‘I do not ask anyone other than Myself concerning My servants. Who is seeking My forgiveness so that I may forgive him? Who is calling upon Me so that I may answer him? Who is asking Me so that I may give him?’
This continues until dawn breaks.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Aḥmad (16215), Ibn Khuzaymah in Kitāb al-Tawḥīd (1/289–291), and Ibn Ḥibbān (212).

٣٠٥ — عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«لولا أن أشق على أمتي لأمرتهم بالسواك عند كل صلاة، ولأخرت العشاء الآخرة إلى ثلث الليل؛ فإنه إذا مضى ثلث الليل الأول هبط الله تبارك وتعالى إلى السماء الدنيا، فلم يزل هنالك حتى يطلع الفجر، يقول:
ألا سائل فيعطى؟ ألا داع فيجاب؟ ألا مستشفع فيشفع؟ ألا تائب مستغفر فيغفر له؟»
حسن: رواه البزار (٤٧٧، ٤٧٨)، وأحمد (٩٦٨)، والدارمي (١٤٩٢)، والدارقطني في النزول (١).

305 — ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Were it not that I would make matters difficult for my Ummah, I would have commanded them to use the siwāk at every prayer, and I would have delayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer until one-third of the night had passed.
For when the first third of the night has passed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, descends to the lowest heaven and remains there until dawn rises, saying:
‘Is there anyone asking so that he may be given? Is there anyone supplicating so that he may be answered? Is there anyone seeking intercession so that intercession may be granted to him? Is there any repentant person seeking forgiveness so that he may be forgiven?’”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Bazzār (477, 478), Aḥmad (968), al-Dārimī (1492), and al-Dāraquṭnī in al-Nuzūl (1).

“Were it not that I would make matters difficult for my Ummah, I would have commanded them to use the siwāk at every prayer, and I would have delayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer until one-third of the night had passed.
For when the first third of the night has passed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, descends to the lowest heaven and remains there until dawn rises, saying:
‘Is there anyone asking so that he may be given? Is there anyone supplicating so that he may be answered? Is there anyone seeking intercession so that intercession may be granted to him? Is there any repentant person seeking forgiveness so that he may be forgiven?’”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Bazzār (477, 478), Aḥmad (968), al-Dārimī (1492), and al-Dāraquṭnī in al-Nuzūl (1).

٣٠٦ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«إذا كان ثلث الليل الباقي، يهبط الله عز وجل إلى السماء الدنيا، ثم تُفتح أبواب السماء، ثم يبسط يده، فيقول:
هل من سائل يعطى سؤله؟
فلا يزال كذلك حتى يطلع الفجر».
حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (٣٦٧٣، ٣٨٢١)، وأبو يعلى (٥٣١٩).

هذه الأحاديث شاملة لنزول الله تبارك وتعالى إلى السماء الدنيا كل ليلة، وأما تخصيص ليلة النصف من شعبان فكلها ضعيفة لا يعول عليها.

٣٠٧ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«فيأتيهم الله في غير الصورة التي يعرفون، فيقول: أنا ربكم.
فيقولون: نعوذ بالله منك، هذا مكاننا حتى يأتينا ربنا، فإذا أتانا ربنا عرفناه.
فيأتيهم الله في الصورة التي يعرفون».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٤٣٧)، ومسلم (١٨٢).

307 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Allah will come to them in a form other than the form in which they recognize Him and will say:
‘I am your Lord.’
They will say:
‘We seek refuge in Allah from you. We will remain here until our Lord comes to us; when our Lord comes to us, we will recognize Him.’
Then Allah will come to them in the form in which they recognize Him.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7437) and Muslim (182).

٣٠٨ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه قال:
كان رسول الله ﷺ يعودني عام حجة الوداع من وجع اشتد بي، فقلت:
يا رسول الله، قد بلغ بي من الوجع ما ترى، وأنا ذو مال، ولا يرثني إلا ابنة لي، أفأتصدق بثلثي مالي؟
قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«لا».
فقلت:
فالشطر؟
قال:
«لا».
ثم قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«الثلث، والثلث كثير. إنك إن تذر ورثتك أغنياء خير من أن تذرهم عالة يتكففون الناس، وإنك لن تنفق نفقة تبتغي بها وجه الله إلا أُجرت، حتى ما تجعل في في امرأتك».
متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٤)، والبخاري (١٢٩٥)، ومسلم (١٦٢٨).

308 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ may Allah be pleased with him reported:
During the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to visit me because of an illness that had become severe.
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, my illness has reached the severity that you see. I possess wealth, and no one will inherit from me except one daughter. Should I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“No.”
I asked:
“Then half?”
He replied:
“No.”
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“One-third, and one-third is much. Indeed, leaving your heirs wealthy is better than leaving them poor and begging from people.
And you will never spend anything seeking thereby the Face of Allah except that you will be rewarded for it, even what you place in your wife’s mouth.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik (4), al-Bukhārī (1295), and Muslim (1628).

٣٠٩ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال:
لما كان يوم حنين آثر أناساً في القسمة، فأعطى الأقرع بن حابس مائة من الإبل، وأعطى عيينة مثل ذلك، وأعطى أناساً من أشراف العرب، فآثرهم يومئذ في القسمة.
فقال رجل:
والله إن هذه القسمة ما عدل فيها، وما أريد بها وجه الله!
فقلت:
والله لأخبرن النبي ﷺ.
فأتيته فأخبرته، فقال:
«فمن يعدل إذا لم يعدل الله ورسوله؟ رحم الله موسى، قد أوذي بأكثر من هذا فصبر».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣١٥٠)، ومسلم (١٠٦٢).

english_source:
309 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd may Allah be pleased with him reported:
On the day of Ḥunayn, the Prophet ﷺ favored certain people in the distribution. He gave al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis one hundred camels, gave ʿUyaynah the same amount, and gave gifts to several of the Arab nobles, favoring them in the distribution that day.
A man said:
“By Allah, there was no justice in this distribution, nor was the Face of Allah sought through it!”
I said:
“By Allah, I will inform the Prophet ﷺ.”
I went to him and informed him.
He said:
“Then who would act justly if Allah and His Messenger did not act justly? May Allah have mercy upon Moses. He was harmed with more than this, yet he remained patient.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3150) and Muslim (1062).

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3150) and Muslim (1062).
full_display_content:
٣٠٩ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال:
لما كان يوم حنين آثر أناساً في القسمة، فأعطى الأقرع بن حابس مائة من الإبل، وأعطى عيينة مثل ذلك، وأعطى أناساً من أشراف العرب، فآثرهم يومئذ في القسمة.
فقال رجل:
والله إن هذه القسمة ما عدل فيها، وما أريد بها وجه الله!
فقلت:
والله لأخبرن النبي ﷺ.
فأتيته فأخبرته، فقال:
«فمن يعدل إذا لم يعدل الله ورسوله؟ رحم الله موسى، قد أوذي بأكثر من هذا فصبر».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣١٥٠)، ومسلم (١٠٦٢).
309 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd may Allah be pleased with him reported:
On the day of Ḥunayn, the Prophet ﷺ favored certain people in the distribution. He gave al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis one hundred camels, gave ʿUyaynah the same amount, and gave gifts to several of the Arab nobles, favoring them in the distribution that day.
A man said:
“By Allah, there was no justice in this distribution, nor was the Face of Allah sought through it!”
I said:
“By Allah, I will inform the Prophet ﷺ.”
I went to him and informed him.
He said:
“Then who would act justly if Allah and His Messenger did not act justly? May Allah have mercy upon Moses. He was harmed with more than this, yet he remained patient.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3150) and Muslim (1062).

٣١٠ — عن عبد الله بن قيس رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«جنتان من فضة، آنيتهما وما فيهما، وجنتان من ذهب، آنيتهما وما فيهما، وما بين القوم وبين أن ينظروا إلى ربهم إلا رداء الكبرياء على وجهه في جنة عدن».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٨٧٨)، ومسلم (١٨٠).

“Two gardens will be of silver, along with their vessels and everything within them; and two gardens will be of gold, along with their vessels and everything within them.
Nothing will stand between the people and their looking upon their Lord except the veil of Majesty over His Face in the Garden of ʿAdn.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4878) and Muslim (180).

arabic_source:
٣١١ — عن عتبان بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال:
غدا عليَّ رسول الله ﷺ، فقال رجل:
أين مالك بن الدخشن؟
فقال رجل منا:
ذلك منافق، لا يحب الله ورسوله.
فقال النبي ﷺ:
«ألا تقولوه! يقول: لا إله إلا الله، يبتغي بذلك وجه الله».
قال:
بلى.
قال:
«فإنه لا يوافي عبد يوم القيامة به إلا حرم الله عليه النار».
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٩٣٨).

311 — ʿItbān ibn Mālik may Allah be pleased with him reported:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me one morning.
A man asked:
“Where is Mālik ibn al-Dukhshun?”
One of us replied:
“He is a hypocrite who does not love Allah and His Messenger.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Do not say that! Does he not say, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah,’ seeking thereby the Face of Allah?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“No servant will come on the Day of Resurrection with that testimony except that Allah will make the Fire forbidden for him.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6938).

٣١٢ — عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنهما قال:
لما نزلت هذه الآية:
﴿قُلْ هُوَ الْقَادِرُ عَلَى أَنْ يَبْعَثَ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابًا مِنْ فَوْقِكُمْ﴾
 [الأنعام: ٦٥]
قال النبي ﷺ:
«أعوذ بوجهك».
قال:
﴿أَوْ مِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ﴾
فقال النبي ﷺ:
«أعوذ بوجهك».
قال:
﴿أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ شِيَعًا﴾
فقال النبي ﷺ:
«هذا أيسر».
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧٤٠٦).

312 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh may Allah be pleased with them reported:
When the verse was revealed:
“Say: He is able to send upon you punishment from above you…”
 [Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:65]
the Prophet ﷺ said:
“I seek refuge in Your Face.”
Then came:
“…or from beneath your feet…”
and the Prophet ﷺ said:
“I seek refuge in Your Face.”
Then came:
“…or to divide you into factions…”
and the Prophet ﷺ said:
“This is easier.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7406).

٣١٣ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه قال:
كنا مع النبي ﷺ ستة نفر، فقال المشركون للنبي ﷺ:
اطرد هؤلاء، لا يجترئون علينا.
قال:
وكنت أنا، وابن مسعود، ورجل من هذيل، وبلال، ورجلان لست أسميهما.
فوقع في نفس رسول الله ﷺ ما شاء الله أن يقع، فحدث نفسه، فأنزل الله عز وجل:
﴿وَلَا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾
 [الأنعام: ٥٢]
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤١٣).

313 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ may Allah be pleased with him reported:
We were with the Prophet ﷺ, six men in all, when the polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ:
“Drive these men away so that they will not dare to sit with us.”
I was among them, along with Ibn Masʿūd, a man from Hudhayl, Bilāl, and two men whose names I will not mention.
Something occurred in the heart of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as Allah willed, and he considered the matter.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then revealed:
“Do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face. You are not accountable for them in anything…”
 [Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:52]
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (2413).

﴿وَلَا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾
 [الأنعام: ٥٢]
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤١٣).
313 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ may Allah be pleased with him reported:
We were with the Prophet ﷺ, six men in all, when the polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ:
“Drive these men away so that they will not dare to sit with us.”
I was among them, along with Ibn Masʿūd, a man from Hudhayl, Bilāl, and two men whose names I will not mention.
Something occurred in the heart of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as Allah willed, and he considered the matter.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then revealed:
“Do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face. You are not accountable for them in anything…”
 [Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:52]
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (2413).

٣١٤ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«إن المرأة عورة، فإذا خرجت استشرفها الشيطان، وأقرب ما تكون من وجه ربها وهي في قعر بيتها».
صحيح: رواه ابن خزيمة في صحيحه (١٦٨٥)، وفي كتاب التوحيد (٢٣)، وعنه ابن حبان (٥٥٩٩).

٣١٥ — عن الحارث الأشعري رضي الله عنه، أن النبي ﷺ قال:
«إن الله أمر يحيى بن زكريا بخمس كلمات أن يعمل بها، ويأمر بني إسرائيل أن يعملوا بها…
وإن الله أمركم بالصلاة، فإذا صليتم فلا تلتفتوا؛ فإن الله ينصب وجهه لوجه عبده في صلاته ما لم يلتفت…»
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٢٨٦٣)، وقال:
«حديث حسن صحيح غريب».

315 — Al-Ḥārith al-Ashʿarī may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Allah commanded Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā with five commands: that he act upon them and command the Children of Israel to act upon them…
And Allah has commanded you to pray. When you pray, do not turn away, for Allah directs His Face toward the face of His servant during his prayer so long as the servant does not turn away…”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2863), who said:
“A Ḥasan Ṣaḥīḥ Gharīb ḥadīth.”

٣١٦ — عن أم سلمة رضي الله عنها أن نبي الله ﷺ قال:
«من أدى زكاة ماله، طيب النفس بها، يريد بها وجه الله والدار الآخرة، لم يغيب شيئاً من ماله، وأقام الصلاة، ثم أدى الزكاة، فتعدى عليه الحق، فأخذ سلاحه فقاتل فقُتل، فهو شهيد».
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٦٥٧٤)، والطبراني في الكبير (٢٣/٢٨٧)، وصححه ابن خزيمة (٢٣٣٦).

316 — Umm Salamah may Allah be pleased with her reported that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever pays the zakāh due upon his wealth willingly and with a content heart, seeking thereby the Face of Allah and the Hereafter, conceals nothing of his wealth, establishes the prayer, and then pays the zakāh; but afterward his right is transgressed against, so he takes up his weapon, fights, and is killed — then he is a martyr.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Aḥmad (26574) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (23/287), and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (2336).

٣١٧ — عن عطاء بن السائب، عن أبيه قال:
صلى بنا عمار بن ياسر رضي الله عنه صلاة فأوجز فيها…
ثم جاء فأخبر به القوم:
«اللهم بعلمك الغيب، وقدرتك على الخلق، أحيني ما علمت الحياة خيراً لي…
وأسألك لذة النظر إلى وجهك، والشوق إلى لقائك، في غير ضراء مضرة، ولا فتنة مضلة.
اللهم زينا بزينة الإيمان، واجعلنا هداة مهتدين».
صحيح: رواه النسائي (١٣٠٥)، والدارمي في الرد على الجهمية (١٨٨).

317 — ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib reported from his father:
ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir may Allah be pleased with him led us in prayer and made it brief…
He then informed the people of the supplication:
“O Allah, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive for as long as You know life to be better for me…
I ask You for the delight of looking upon Your Face and for longing to meet You, without harmful adversity and without a misleading trial.
O Allah, adorn us with the adornment of faith and make us rightly guided guides.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (1305) and al-Dārimī in al-Radd ʿalā al-Jahmiyyah (188).

arabic_source:
٣١٨ — عن أبي مسعود الأنصاري رضي الله عنه قال:
كنت أضرب غلاماً لي، فسمعت من خلفي صوتاً لا أعلمه:
«أبا مسعود! الله أقدر عليك منك عليه».
فالتفت فإذا هو رسول الله ﷺ.
فقلت:
يا رسول الله، هو حر لوجه الله.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ:
«أما لو لم تفعل للفحتك النار، أو لمستك النار».
صحيح: رواه مسلم في الأيمان والنذور (١٦٥٨: ٣٥).

318 — Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī may Allah be pleased with him reported:
I was striking a servant of mine when I heard a voice behind me that I did not recognize:
“O Abū Masʿūd! Allah has more power over you than you have over him.”
I turned around and found that it was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, he is free for the Face of Allah.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Had you not done so, the Fire would have scorched you — or the Fire would have touched you.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim in al-Aymān wa al-Nudhūr (1658:35).

319 — Ṣuhayb may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“For those who do good is the best reward and an increase.”
 [Sūrat Yūnus 10:26]
He said:
“The increase is looking upon the Face of our Lord, Mighty and Majestic.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa al-Ṣifāt (665).
Hannād ibn al-Sarī also narrated it in al-Zuhd (171) with the wording:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited:
“For those who do good is the best reward and an increase.”
Then he said:
“When the people of Paradise have entered Paradise and the people of the Fire have entered the Fire, a caller will call:
‘O people of Paradise, you have an appointment with Allah which He intends to fulfill for you.’
They will say:
‘What is it? Has Allah not made our scales heavy, brightened our faces, admitted us into Paradise, and saved us from the Fire?’
Then the veil will be removed and He will manifest Himself, and they will look upon Him.
By Allah, He will not have given them anything more beloved to them than looking upon Him — and that is the increase.”
The basis of this ḥadīth is found in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (181), where the wording is:
“Looking upon their Lord, Mighty and Majestic.”
The word “Face” is not mentioned in that version.

«ما بعث الله من نبي إلا أنذر قومه الأعور الكذاب، وإنه أعور، وإن ربكم ليس بأعور، مكتوب بين عينيه: كافر».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٤٠٨)، ومسلم (٢٩٣٣).

320 — Anas may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Allah did not send any prophet except that he warned his people of the one-eyed liar. Indeed, he is one-eyed, while your Lord is not one-eyed. Written between his eyes is: ‘Disbeliever.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7408) and Muslim (2933).

٣٢٤ — عن أبي يونس سليم بن جبير، مولى أبي هريرة، قال:
سمعت أبا هريرة يقرأ هذه الآية:
﴿إِنَّ اللهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا﴾
إلى قوله:
﴿إِنَّ اللهَ كَانَ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا﴾
 [النساء: ٥٨]
قال:
رأيت رسول الله ﷺ يضع إبهامه على أذنه، والتي تليها على عينه.
قال أبو هريرة:
رأيت رسول الله ﷺ يقرؤها ويضع إصبعيه.
قال ابن يونس:
قال المقرئ: يعني أن الله سميع بصير؛ يعني أن لله سمعاً وبصراً.
قال أبو داود:
«وهذا رد على الجهمية».
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٤٧٢٨)، وصححه ابن خزيمة وأخرجه في كتاب التوحيد (٤٩).

324 — Abū Yūnus Sulaym ibn Jubayr, the freedman of Abū Hurayrah, reported:
I heard Abū Hurayrah reciting the verse:
“Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to those to whom they are due…”
until the words:
“Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.”
 [Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:58]
He said:
“I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ place his thumb upon his ear and the finger next to it upon his eye.”
Abū Hurayrah said:
“I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reciting the verse and placing his two fingers.”
Ibn Yūnus said:
The reciter explained that Allah is Hearing and Seeing; that is, Allah possesses hearing and sight.
Abū Dāwūd said:
“This is a refutation of the Jahmiyyah.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4728), and authenticated and narrated by Ibn Khuzaymah in Kitāb al-Tawḥīd (49).

٣٢٥ — عن أم سلمة زوج النبي ﷺ قالت:
ذكرت المسيح الدجال ليلة، فلم يأتني النوم، فلما أصبحت دخلت على رسول الله ﷺ فأخبرته، فقال:
«لا تفعلي؛ فإنه إن يخرج وأنا حي يكفيكموه الله بي، وإن يخرج بعد أن أموت يكفيكموه الله بالصالحين».
ثم قال:
«ما من نبي إلا وقد حذر أمته الدجال، وإني أحذركموه. إنه أعور، وإن الله ليس بأعور. إنه يمشي في الأرض، وإن الأرض والسماء لله. ألا إن المسيح الدجال عينه اليمنى كأنها عنبة طافية».
حسن: رواه ابن خزيمة في التوحيد (٥٦).

325 — Umm Salamah may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, reported:
One night I thought about the False Messiah, the Dajjāl, and sleep would not come to me.
When morning came, I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him.
He said:
“Do not do that. If he emerges while I am alive, Allah will suffice you against him through me; and if he emerges after I die, Allah will suffice you against him through the righteous.”
Then he said:
“There was no prophet except that he warned his nation about the Dajjāl, and I am warning you about him. He is one-eyed, whereas Allah is not one-eyed. He walks upon the earth, while the earth and the heaven belong to Allah. Be aware that the right eye of the False Messiah, the Dajjāl, is like a floating grape.”
Ḥasan: Narrated by Ibn Khuzaymah in al-Tawḥīd (56).

٣٢٦ — عن أسماء بنت يزيد رضي الله عنها:
أن رسول الله ﷺ جلس مجلساً مرة يحدثهم عن أعور الدجال، فكان مما ذكر فيه:
«فمن حضر مجلسي، وسمع قولي، فليبلغ الشاهد منكم الغائب، واعلموا أن الله عز وجل صحيح ليس بأعور، وأن الدجال أعور مسوح العين، بين عينيه مكتوب كافر، يقرؤه كل مؤمن كاتب وغير كاتب».

٣٢٧ — عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنهما، في حديث طويل في خروج الدجال، وفيه:
«فيقول للناس: أنا ربكم، وهو أعور، وإن ربكم ليس بأعور».
حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (١٤٩٥٤)، وصححه ابن خزيمة في كتاب التوحيد (٥٥)، والحاكم (٤/٥٣٠).
قال الإمام الدارمي في الرد على المريسي (١/٣٢٧):
«ففي تأويل قول رسول الله ﷺ: إن الله ليس بأعور، بيان أنه ذو عينين خلاف الأعور».
